# 10 — Roadmap and Task List

Ordering reflects the owner's priorities: **performance → observability → Kubernetes + Pi deployability → clustering/HA → breadth**. Each task lists the requirement IDs it satisfies and objective acceptance criteria (AC). A task is done only when its AC pass in CI. Tick boxes as you go and keep this file current.

**Every surface ships with its UI (owner rule 2026-11-16; API-901, ADR-914).** Every task that adds a setting, route or tool ships its UI control, help topic and Playwright test in the same task; a task without them isn't done. Exceptions are inherently offline commands, each with a one-line reason. The control is a form field, page, card or action. Role gating matches the API and is enforced by the server: viewers read, and operators or admins change. Each control has a `?` help topic that passes `check:help`, and at least one Playwright test names it (mocking API answers with `page.route` where the e2e server has no such source). A credential is only ever entered through `SecretField` (write-only, never shown or pre-filled; ADR-903 §9), and a `<redacted>` value is never shown as if it were the value. Security gates and bootstrap settings (keys, listeners, API address and TLS, trusted proxies, cluster init and join) get admin controls with the guardrails of ADR-914: admin only on the server, never agents, a typed confirmation, audit, and an automatic rollback for address changes; a key is never typed into the store it protects. A node-local section (`shared.rs` `NODE_LOCAL`) becomes editable only through `node_managed` (T23.10), as an entry for the node it applies to. The file wins over every UI value and is shown as "set by file". A task that adds no setting, route or tool (a deploy bundle, a benchmark, an internal fix, an outside integration) says "No UI: <reason>". This applies to all wave work, including tasks already ticked in M22 and M24, which T24.12–T24.18 catch up; M27 catches up the pre-fork features.

**Upstream (fork rule).** The fork's differences from `paimonsoror/telltaledns`, its last sync, the sync procedure and the upstream issues it triages are in [`spec/upstream.md`](upstream.md). The on-demand watch workflow (`upstream-watch.yml`, dispatch only since ADR-1026) was removed on 2026-11-20 by owner decision (ADR-1073); `.github/scripts/upstream_watch.py` remains. Upstream ADR numbers are kept; fork ADRs take 901 and up; colliding milestone or task IDs are renamed (M22/M23 became M28/M29 at the 2026-11-17 merge).

## M1 — Fast forwarding resolver (weeks 2–4)
- [x] **T1.1 wrendns-proto hot path.** Header/question/OPT parse, name normalization + hash, response TTL-offset scan, ID/TTL patching, synthesis helpers (NXDOMAIN/NODATA/A/AAAA/EDE). *(DNS-005, DNS-013, DNS-019)* *AC:* proptest round-trips; fuzz target runs for 10 min clean; differential test vs hickory. *Done 2026-10-02: 2000-case proptests + hickory 0.26 differential both directions; 3 fuzz targets × 10 min, 0 crashes (69.9M execs). Micro-bench (x86 WSL): parse+hash 53 ns, blocked answer 56 ns, cache-hit patch 5 ns.*
- [x] **T1.2 UDP workers.** SO_REUSEPORT per worker, recvmmsg/sendmmsg, PKTINFO. *(DNS-001)* *AC:* answers `kdig`; multi-core scaling test shows ≥ 3.2× qps at 4 workers vs 1. *Done 2026-10-02: verified with `dig` (kdig not installed; equivalent). `examples/udp_scaling`: 3.58× at 4 workers with 20 µs/query synthetic work. With 2 µs/query the in-process generator saturates first (2.16×), so the authoritative number must come from the dnsperf harness (T0.3) on separate hardware. Non-Linux fallback compiles but is untested here.*
- [x] **T1.3 TCP listener.** Pipelining, limits, idle timeouts. *(DNS-001)* *Done 2026-10-02: RFC 7766 pipelining (reader/writer split, ready for out-of-order async replies), 10 s idle timeout, 64 in-flight per connection, 1024 connection cap (constants for now; config keys come with T1.10/OPS tuning). Per-thread response scratch keeps idle connections cheap.*
- [x] **T1.4 Cache.** Sharded S3-FIFO, wire storage, TTL clamps, negative caching, singleflight. *(DNS-006)* *AC:* zero-alloc test passes (NFR-002); hit ratio on the Zipf corpus ≥ LRU baseline. *Done 2026-10-02: 0 allocations over 100k hits + 100k blocked answers. S3-FIFO vs LRU (100k names, 1M Zipf requests): s=1.0 59.7%/50.5% (1% cache), 77.8%/73.4% (10%); s=0.8 31.4%/20.4%, 54.5%/46.6%. Full hit path 153 ns single-thread. Also includes serve-stale lookup (DNS-007) and the prefetch signal (DNS-008); the background refresh itself lands with upstreams. Not wired into `wrendns run` until T1.5. Decision: negative answers without SOA are not cached (RFC 2308 §5); responses whose OPT isn't the last record are not cached.*
- [x] **T1.5 Upstreams v1.** UDP/TCP/DoT/DoH(h2) transports with pooling; strategies (failover, round_robin, weighted, fastest, parallel); health + breaker; bootstrap; loop detection. *(UPS-001, 005, 006, 008, 009)* *AC:* chaos test with toxiproxy: one upstream at 100% loss → no client-visible failures; p99 within 1.5× of the healthy baseline. *Progress 2026-10-02 — **T1.5a done**: UDP (+TCP fallback on TC) and TCP transports with anti-spoofing validation; all five strategies; health (EWMA, 50-sample window, breaker) and active checks; 2 s budget; hedged attempts (ADR-013); routes; pipeline wired with cache, singleflight, serve-stale, prefetch, SERVFAIL+EDE. Chaos AC met in-process (fake upstreams, one blackholed): 0 failures, p99 1.04–1.15× baseline across failover/round_robin/fastest/parallel; toxiproxy version pending Docker. Verified live against 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9 with a dead member. **T1.5b done**: DoT and DoH (HTTP/2) over rustls (ring, Mozilla roots built in), pooled pipelined TCP/DoT connections with ID demux, h2 multiplexing, bootstrap resolution for hostnames (per-upstream servers or /etc/resolv.conf minus our listeners), loop tag (EDNS 65429) with drop + error log. Verified live: DoT 1.1.1.1, DoH dns.quad9.net and dns.google. Not yet: spki_pins, proxy, ECS, DoH3 (startup errors if configured).*

## M3 — Observability core + API + auth (weeks 6–9)
- [x] **T3.1 QueryEvent rings + aggregator + rollups + top-K + HDR.** *(OBS-001, 002, 004)* *AC:* drop counter is 0 at 100k qps sustained on x86 with default ring sizes. *Done 2026-10-03: `wrendns_telemetry` `event` (QueryEvent / UpstreamEvent records with the full lowercased qname), `ring::Hub` (per-thread wait-free `rtrb` byte rings, registered on first use, per-ring emitted/dropped counters, wall clock derived from the query's `Instant`), the aggregator thread (25 ms drains) and `agg::Aggregates` (per-second 15 min and per-minute 48 h windows by status/qtype/rcode/proto/group/upstream; Space-Saving top-K over an indexed min-heap for domains, blocked, NXDOMAIN, clients, and per-client domains for the 64 most recent clients; HDR latency by path×proto, qtype, client (256 + other), upstream stage, and upstream; current + previous hour). The pipeline emits on every answer (sync, drops, deferred) with client, group, status, rcode, flags, timings, and FLT-013 rule attribution for blocks, allows, and CNAME blocks; `resolve_upstream` emits UpstreamEvents. `wrendns_telemetry_{events,dropped}_total{ring}` metrics; `bench.py sustain`. **AC met** on the homelab: 99,991 qps sustained for 60 s, 6.0M events, **0 dropped**, RSS 41 MiB. A/B: p50/p99 at 50% load unchanged (34 / 751 µs), saturated cache-hot qps −2.4% / −3.7% in two A/Bs, within run-to-run spread. Default `ring_slots` 65,536 → 4,096, 2-digit HDR, byte records: ADR-026 (Proposed). Deferred to T3.2: interning, SQLite rollup persistence (`06` §3); `QueryEvent.upstream` (upstream analytics come from UpstreamEvents); stage timings for filter/cache (sub-µs, not worth two clock reads per query yet).*

The load client asks one server, waits 0.4 s, then asks the other; step 2 stopped the primary the moment the restarted replica answered the script's probe, while a client query that began while the replica was still down was waiting out its timeout, so for that one query both servers were down (the failed run lost 1 of 1297, at the step 2 to 3 hand-over). `upgrade-e2e.sh` now stops the next node only after the load client itself was answered by the node just restarted (`served_since`). Run in the build container with this build as both N and N-1 under CPU load: no query was lost in the 5 of 8 runs that reached the final count (the other 3 failed earlier, at the replica's join of the old primary or the canary sync, under up to 48 busy loops; not fixed here), and the failure itself was not reproduced before it (it needs a restart longer than the 0.4 s timeout), so the cause rests on the CI log's timestamps. *Open:* the join retry and canary-sync flake under heavy load. The "pinned: SERVFAIL 7.4% ... (limit 5.0%)" and "canary SERVFAIL 145 of 1752" lines in that job's log belong to the earlier step `rollout-e2e.sh`, which passed (it injects those failures on purpose).*

## M6 — Protocol depth + migration (weeks 13–16)
- [x] **T6.1 DNSSEC validation + NTAs + EDE.** *(DNS-011)* *Done 2026-10-05 (ADR-060):*
  - *`[dnssec] mode = off|validate|permissive`, off by default until soaked. Negative trust anchors, including routes with `dnssec_nta`.*
  - *hickory-net's validating handle runs over our upstream groups (DO and CD upstream, per-group validation cache).*
  - *AD for secure answers to clients that ask. Bogus answers become SERVFAIL with EDE 6, never stale or cached. CD bypasses validation. DNSSEC records are stripped for clients without DO.*
  - *`wrendns_dnssec_validation_total{result}`.*
  - *Fixed for all queries: a truncated UDP answer's TCP retry now gets its own timeout.*
  - *`deploy/dnssec-e2e.sh` (CI, real DNS tree): secure, insecure, bogus, CD, and signed denials.*
  - *Deferred: RFC 5011, RFC 8198, per-reason EDE codes, query-event field, Settings UI.*
- [x] **T6.2 Serve-stale, prefetch, cache persistence.** *(DNS-007, 008, 009)* *Done 2026-10-05:*
  - *Serve-stale (RFC 8767, EDE 3) and prefetch were already in the cache and pipeline.*
  - *New: `[cache] persist`. The cache is dumped to `<data_dir>/cache.bin` on shutdown (owner-only) and reloaded on start.*
  - *Entries are re-keyed for the new process's hash seed, aged by the downtime, and only those still servable are kept. A dump from different upstreams or routes (a config fingerprint) is refused. The file is removed once loaded.*
  - *Tests: dump and reload across seeds, expiry, foreign fingerprint, and garbage input. A live restart's first query was a cache hit.*
  - *bench-smoke: cache-hot 139.7k qps, inside the 112–166k range of earlier runs; the hit path is untouched.*
- [x] **T6.3 Pi-hole importer (v5 + v6 Teleporter).** *(API-007)* *Done 2026-10-05 (ADR-061):*
  - *`wrendns import pihole PATH [-o FILE]` reads a v6 zip, a v5 tar.gz, a directory, or a `gravity.db` (zip/tar.gz readers on `miniz_oxide`; SQLite via `rusqlite`, both already in the tree).*
  - *It maps upstreams, conditional forwarding (domain plus reverse zones, with an NTA), local DNS and CNAME records, adlists (v6 allowlists too), exact and regex domains (per set of groups), groups (exact list sets; disabled groups get none), clients, DHCP reservations as named devices, DNSSEC, the rate limit, and the blocking mode.*
  - *The report names every unmapped setting: v6 `### CHANGED` keys, v5 keys. Values are never copied.*
  - *Tests: unit tests on both formats; `deploy/pihole-import-e2e.sh` in CI exports from the official v6 (FTL 6.7.1) and v5 (5.18.3) images and checks the served answers.*
  - *Found by the e2e and fixed: the first blocking snapshot waited for every list's first fetch, so a dead adlist URL (retrying with backoff) delayed all blocking. The fetcher now tells the compiler 10 s after the first update at the latest, without waiting for the rest of the round (`flt_004_a_slow_list_does_not_delay_the_others`).*
  - *Open: a UI/API import (with T6.7 restore).*

Technitium exports: $ORIGIN/$TTL, parentheses, relative names, A/AAAA/CNAME/PTR/TXT/MX/SRV; SOA/NS and unsupported types reported; output validated as config); used to move the owner's `home.example` zone. ADR-041 (Proposed). Open: forwarders and conditional forwarders, block/allow lists, reading from the Technitium API directly.*
  - *Done 2026-10-05 (ADR-062): `wrendns import technitium URL` reads a running server through its API (token from `TECHNITIUM_TOKEN` or `--token-file`). Technitium's backup files are a private binary format.*
  - *It maps forwarders (UDP/TCP/TLS/HTTPS, pinned addresses, concurrent → parallel), primary zones' records, forwarder zones → routes (NTA unless validated), block-list URLs (`!` = allow), blocked/allowed zones, and Advanced Blocking groups (catch-all network → `default`, other networks → `networks`, shared URL lists, regexes).*
  - *Also: the bypass list → a no-list group, the blocking answer, DHCP reservations → devices, DNSSEC, the per-address rate limit, and the saved cache.*
  - *The report covers secondary/stub zones, QUIC forwarders, listener-based groups, per-list answers, the DHCP server, encrypted listeners, ACLs, TSIG, and other apps.*
  - *Tests: unit tests, and `deploy/technitium-import-e2e.sh` in CI against `technitium/dns-server:15.6.0` (it found and fixed a one-forwarder `parallel` bug).*

- [x] **T6.12 Quick rules: per-device and per-group allow/block, optionally expiring (proposed, owner request 2026-10-05).** For everyday cases:
  - unblock a game's server for one person's phone for two hours;
  - block a site for the kids' devices until tomorrow.

  *(FLT-005, FLT-006, FLT-013, AGT-004; a proposed ADR covers precedence and expiry)*
  - **A rule:**
    - allow or block a domain and its subdomains;
    - for chosen devices, groups, or everyone;
    - optional expiry (a duration or a time) and a note;
    - who made it and when.
  - **Storage:** rules are stored like other UI-managed entries (ADR-040) and replicated as shared configuration in a cluster.
  - **Matching:** applied through the matcher's manual-rules overlay, so a new rule takes effect immediately without recompiling the lists. Precedence: device rule > group rule > lists.
  - **Expiry:** enforced on the server when the rule expires; the audit log records adds, removals, and expiries.
  - **Surfaces:**
    - the query log ("Allow for this device: 1 hour / today / always", "Block for this device / group");
    - a device's page ("Block a site…");
    - a Rules page (active rules with a countdown, remove);
    - "Why?" and explain name the rule ("allowed by a quick rule for Mom's phone, expires 21:30");
    - the API and an agent scope, `config:write:rules`, so agents can do it with a reason header and impact estimate.
  - **Docs set honest limits:**
    - DNS sees whole sites (domains), not pages;
    - an app uses many domains (bundles come with FLT-012);
    - a rule follows the device only as well as the device is recognised (DHCP reservation; "private Wi-Fi address" off);
    - devices keep cached answers for a few minutes;
    - mobile data, VPNs, or hard-coded DNS bypass it unless the router blocks outside DNS.
  - **Not parental controls:** no screen time. *(Amended 2026-11-18, ADR-994: content categories are now in scope, FLT-901 and FLT-902, T24.29.)*

  - **Safety: one process per data directory.** On start a node takes an exclusive lock on its data directory. A second process pointing at the same directory refuses to start with a clear message. This guards the real risk of scaling a single-volume Deployment: shared identity, `state.db`, and query-log files across replicas.

## M7 — v1.x (post-1.0, priority order)
MCP write tools with plan/apply + approval inbox, OAuth via OIDC, resources/prompts (AGT-007, 008, 010, 011) → DoQ + DoH3 listeners and upstreams (DNS-004, UPS-002) → schedules, safe search, services (FLT-010..012) → analytics suite + alerts (OBS-009, 010) → recursive resolver (DNS-012, UPS-012) → socket/exec upstream plugins + proxies (UPS-010, 011) → OTLP + dnstap + sinks (OBS-006, 007) → DHCP (OPS-008) → ECS/DNS64/local zones/rewrites/IP filter (DNS-015, 016, 018, FLT-014, 015) → DNSCrypt (UPS-003) → CLI (API-008).

Owner decision 2026-10-06: finish M6, then M7, before a v1.0 release.

Immediate, audited: `flush_cache`, `pause_blocking`, `resume_blocking`.

After the earlier steps (one allocation per cache entry, the index replacing the FST pages) two things were left: mimalloc kept freed pages for its 10 ms purge delay (a compile's churn stayed resident), and about 15 MiB of the executable's code stayed resident after running once (start-up, the API router and OpenAPI document, a compile). Now mimalloc purges at once and the executable's read-only, unmodified pages are released 15 s after start-up and after each filter index build (ADR-144). Idle 13.7 MiB (16.1 after 3 min), 1M names + 100k entries 60.0 MiB (60.9 after 3 min), compile peak 97.5 MiB (was 170). The heap that remains: the cache (about 23 MiB per 100k entries: answers 9, hash tables 10, FIFOs 4), the lookup index (10 MiB per 1M names), telemetry rings (2 MiB).
  - *Findings 2026-10-07 (`bench/memprobe.py`: RSS by mapping next to the server's counters):* idle is **18.8 MiB with the shipped binary** (v0.1.0, musl, fat LTO): 14.2 MiB of it is the binary's own code pages, 4.4 MiB heap. The gate run's 25.2 MiB was the bench build (more code). With 1M names + 100k entries the shipped binary used 111.7 MiB: code ~15, heap ~96, of which the lookup index 10.2, the FSTs read into memory ~9, the cache ~30 (312 B per entry, where the byte budget counted 208), the query log's open dictionary ~10 (capped at 65,536 names per part), and ~20 still unattributed.
  - *Done so far:* cache entries in one allocation, an epoch-relative timestamp, and a byte budget that counts real memory (`tests/footprint.rs`: 312 → 260 B per entry, budget within 5 %; 4-thread hits 12.7 % faster, single-thread unchanged). The domain FSTs are memory-mapped (`wrendns_net::MappedFile`, the only new `unsafe`, in `sys`) and their pages dropped after the hash check and again once the lookup index answers (−9.2 MiB heap at 1M names; ~25 MiB on a Pi with 2.7M).
  - *Heap profile (`bench/heapprof.py`, a `dhat-heap` build):* the "unattributed" memory was a 64 KiB response buffer each query held while waiting upstream (12.5 MiB with 200 in flight), left resident in the allocator after a burst. It's now allocated once the answer is in, sized to it (100k-fill stage 101.4 → 85.0 MiB). The query log's dictionary cap went from 65,536 to 16,384 names per part (its table was 4 MiB at the old cap).
  - *Status 2026-10-07 (bench build):* 1M names + 100k entries 130.4 → **84.2 MiB**; the Pi with 2.7M names 82.8 → **49.6 MiB** (edge 185). Gate: 64 MiB.
  - *Next:* the cache's hash tables and queues (~14 MiB at 100k entries: a 32-byte key in the map and both queues, power-of-two growth), and the binary's code (~15 MiB resident).
- [x] **T10.3 Recompile on a Pi 4 within 8 s.** *(FLT-003)* 2M names take 11.6 s on the single recompile thread; measure 2 threads at `SCHED_IDLE` under load (p99 regression ≤ 10 %), or make the single-thread compile faster.
  - *Progress 2026-10-17:* 2 threads cost more p99 during a recompile on 4 cores (`bench.py swap --server-cpus 0-3 --client-cpus 4-7`: 40.5 → 54 µs vs 44 → 49.5 µs on 1 thread), so the owner kept 1 thread and asked for a faster compile. A parser fast path for the usual line shapes (`name`, `0.0.0.0 name`, `||name^`; the same result as the general parser, tested on the bench lists) cut the parser by a third. On the live Pi (owner's OK, once, in RAM at background priority; DNS answered throughout), the gate's 2M names: 14.2 → 11.8 s on 1 thread, 9.7 s on 2. Building the FST alone takes 8.1 s on one Pi core (the `fst` crate's builder, about 4 µs a name), so a one-thread compile can't meet 8 s while the new filter waits for the FST. The owner chose the first: since ADR-145 the compile's first merge pass fills the lookup index and the new rules serve from it (a pending snapshot), and a second pass writes the FSTs; the finished snapshot reuses the index, and a compile that fails after going live puts the previous filter back (`flt_003_the_live_matcher_decides_like_the_finished_snapshot`, `flt_003_a_recompile_goes_live_before_its_snapshot_is_finished`, `flt_003_sources_rewind_for_a_second_pass`). VM, one thread, 2.74M real names: rules answer at 1.98 s, the compile finishes at 4.55 s (peak 170 MiB, was 163); p99 during a recompile on 4 cores 44.5 → 53 µs (within this harness's noise of the 1-thread baseline). On the live Pi (the owner's OK for a second run; in RAM at background priority, DNS answered throughout), the gate's 2M names on one thread: the new rules answer at 4.77 and 4.71 s; the compile finishes at 12.8 s in the background. **Met** (the gate is measured to when the recompiled filter answers, ADR-145).
- [x] **T10.4 Cold start under 500 ms with the snapshot on disk.** *(NFR-001)* 565 ms until blocking works with 1M names: find what runs between ready (53 ms) and the index being built, and serve from the snapshot sooner.
  - *Done 2026-10-17:* the 565 ms was the measurement. `gate.py` waited for the lookup index (`wrendns_filter_lookup_index_bytes > 0`), polled every 0.5 s, but the node blocks before the index exists: the snapshot is served through the FST walk at once, and the index replaces it when built. Measured as the gate states it (until a blocked name is answered blocked, over DNS every 5 ms, a new name each time so the cache can't hide it), the shipped build blocks 52 ms after starting with 1M names (median of 5; ready 51.5 ms; the index at about 0.5 s). `bench/coldstart.py` measures it and checks the detector against names not on the lists; `gate.py` reports blocking and index times apart.
- [ ] **T10.5 Measurements on separate hardware.** *(NFR-001)* p99 at 50 % load (cache hit, blocked) with the load generator on another machine; Pi 4 throughput on a Pi that isn't serving the home network; cross-site config propagation p95. Needs hardware or the owner's OK for the live cluster.
  - *Progress 2026-10-18 (owner's setup: load from the build VM against a temporary pod on the homelab node, not the live service, no load on the Pi):* a pod in its own namespace (`wrendns-bench`, host network on spare ports, 4 CPUs, 1M names, a loopback stub upstream, the API off, only the VM allowed, rate limiting off), removed afterwards. `bench/remote.py` finds the saturating rate, runs at half, and reads the server's latency histogram around the run: cache hit 99.999 % and blocked 99.999 % of queries within 250 µs (p99 ≤ 50 µs), 0 lost, so **both latency gates are met**; dnsperf's end-to-end p99 (4.9 ms / 455 µs) is the network between the machines. The live service, probed from the homelab host throughout: 1,085 of 1,085 answered, p99 as before the load. **Open:** Pi 4 throughput (owner: no spare Pi, stays unproven); cross-site propagation p95 (read-only from both nodes' logs: 17–32 ms steady, 2.2 s during a primary restart, too few versions yet).
  - *Checked 2026-11-25 (report only):* no new measurement on separate hardware is recorded since the 2026-10-18 progress note; left open.
- [x] **T10.6 Requirement check.** Every P0 requirement in `spec/01` against its test or evidence.
  - *Done 2026-10-17:* `spec/trace.py` (Rust tests named after the requirement, Playwright titles, `REQ:` marks in end-to-end scripts and CI, `spec/trace-evidence.toml` for what a test can't show) writes `docs/v1-requirements.md`; `--check` runs in CI's `site` job and the VM gate, failing on a stale report or a P0 without evidence. Result: 73 P0s, 66 with named tests, all with evidence. Gaps found and closed: DNS-017 (reverse-zone routing over the private-PTR rule: `dns_017_reverse_zone_goes_to_its_route`), OPS-006 (`ops_006_health_endpoints` through the router), NFR-003 (`nfr_003_unsafe_is_forbidden_outside_wrendns_net`), DNS-013's EDE 22 (`dns_013_no_upstream_answer_is_servfail_with_ede_22`), NFR-007's store write latency and segment count (new `wrendns_qlog_block_write_seconds`, `wrendns_qlog_segments`; `nfr_007_store_write_latency_and_segment_count`). **Open:** NFR-005 (T10.10). T10.8 decided by the owner: our own numbers and method only.
- [x] **T10.10 Supply chain.** *(NFR-005)* `cargo-auditable` release builds, a CycloneDX SBOM per release, cosign-signed images (keyless, GitHub OIDC), and a reproducibility check (two builds of the same commit compared).
  - *Done 2026-10-18 (ADR-146):* the Dockerfile builds with `cargo auditable zigbuild` (pinned, checksummed), and the image workflow checks every binary has the `.dep-v0` section; `syft` (pinned) writes a CycloneDX SBOM per binary from that data, checked by `deploy/release/sbom_check.py` (303 components for amd64) and covered by the signed `SHA256SUMS`; every pushed image (edge, release tags) is signed by digest with keyless cosign and the signature verified in the same step (`.github/scripts/cosign-sign.sh`; `verify.sh` checks it for stable releases); the nightly `reproducible` job builds the amd64 release binary twice without cache and compares. Two clean builds first differed (mimalloc's `__TIME__`): the build date is now the commit's and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is passed to the build. On the VM, two uncached builds then came out identical. User docs: "Checking what you run" in `docs/running.md`.
- [x] **T10.7 Security review.** Sign-in (local and OIDC), the cluster channel (mTLS, join, forwarding, failover), and the parsers (DNS wire, lists, config, the query log).
  - *Done 2026-10-17:* `docs/security-review.md`. Fixed, each with a test: unknown cluster members trusted at their word (C1, high), RPC answers accepted from any stream (C2, high), votes for ineligible candidates, users and tokens sent to resolver pods, peer simulations naming local files, unbounded shipped uploads and joins (ADR-143); account changes with any credential (owner: signed-in sessions only), self-service password checks outside the lockout, replica sessions outliving a password change, half-made tokens (ADR-142); the dotted-label filter bypass, query-log dictionary inflation, damaged anomaly state, backup restore paths, zip totals, short cache-dump questions. **Deferred:** fuzz targets for the cluster frame decoder, the backup and import archive readers, and the cache dump loader. **Before rollout:** check (read-only) that each live node's registry lists every node.
- [x] **T10.9 DNSSEC: insecure delegations reached through CNAMEs (found in a live trial).** *(DNS-011, ADR-098)* hickory 0.26 judges answers in unsigned zones reached through CNAMEs as bogus (`www.netflix.com`: EDE 10) or loops on NS/DS lookups (`prod.ftl.netflix.com`). Before accepting a bogus verdict, check whether an ancestor of each name in the chain is provably unsigned (a secure denial of its DS at the parent); if so, the answer is insecure. Tests on real chains; a bug report for hickory. *Done 2026-10-07:* the depth limit is indeterminate, bogus names are logged in permissive mode, hickory's validator log is off, and replicas no longer repeat config warnings on every applied change (cad423f). Then `Validator::proven_insecure`: walking down from the domain under the TLD, the first apex (own SOA) whose DS denial validates (secure, or insecure for NSEC3 opt-out) makes the zone unsigned; a bogus verdict, an error, or a timeout becomes insecure if every owner in the answer is in such a zone; proven zones cached 15 minutes (4,096 at most) and not validated again. Tests: `dns_011_zone_candidates`, `dns_011_offline_unsigned_zone_through_cname_is_insecure` (the test root delegates an unsigned `u.` with a CNAME chain). Live, Quad9, `validate` mode: Netflix, Amazon, BBC, Apple names resolve (insecure); `isc.org`, `example.com` secure with AD; `dnssec-failed.org` SERVFAIL. A bug report for hickory is drafted (`hickory` judges such answers bogus although it validates the parent's DS denial). Also: hickory's `DnsError::Nsec` (a negative answer with a non-secure proof) is read for the DS denial (NSEC3 opt-out is `Insecure`); the stream pool retries a query once on a fresh connection when the server closes the connection before answering (`tests/pool_retry.rs`; before, only a closed-before-sending connection was retried); each pooled connection logs why it ended (debug); `WRENDNS_LOG_DNSSEC_LIBRARY=1` turns hickory's validator log back on. **Still open:** at a cold start Quad9 sometimes closes fresh DoT connections with queries unanswered, which can make the first validations fail (signed zones bogus for a while); `permissive` stays the recommendation until that's understood (next: failure reasons in `wrendns_upstream_requests_total`).
- [x] **T10.8 Comparative report.** Owner decision: publish our own numbers and method only, or change the gate. *Decided 2026-10-17 (owner):* our own numbers and the exact method only, no side-by-side with other resolvers; `docs/v1-gate.md` and `site/performance.html` are that report.

Everything runs on the telemetry thread, a background task, or the asynchronous upstream path; the cache-hit and blocked-answer paths don't change.

- [x] **T9.1 Users and tokens across the cluster.** *(CLU-003, API-003; ADR-045)* Users, recovery codes, and API/agent tokens made on the primary work on every node; replicas refuse identity changes with a pointer to the primary.

  - *AC:* merged percentiles equal those of one histogram with every value; older peers still count (approximate blend, not missing); a query on the replica appears in the primary's live tail within seconds, labelled with its node; `scope=node:local` keeps the tail local; idle remote sessions close.

## M13 — Operations pack (owner request 2026-10-09)
From the capability review of 2026-10-09: the owner picked four of the proposals. Same condition as M11: nothing on the cache-hit or blocked-answer path; everything runs on the telemetry thread, a background task, the cluster channel, or the API. Each task has an opinionated design doc in `docs/design/` that the implementing agent follows; deviations go into the task's ADR as amendments. Suggested order: T13.4 (smallest, exercises heartbeat fields and health plumbing) → T13.1 → T13.3 → T13.2 (largest; builds on T13.1's `impact` for the pin diff and on T13.4's heartbeat changes).

- [x] **T13.1 Change simulation.** *(OBS-024, AGT-002, ADR-115; design `docs/design/change-simulation.md`)* `simulate=<window>` on every dry run adds `impact` (newly blocked / newly allowed / changed route / changed answer, by device and name, rows, partial); `POST /api/v1/simulate` for a whole candidate shared configuration and `wrendns config simulate`; MCP `simulate_change`, `plan_*` tools take `simulate` and carry `impact` only when asked or when `plans_by_default` is on (owner 2026-10-09); the UI's `ChangePreview` gains a "What would this have done?" button; `[simulate]` as a shared one-of section with Settings → System → *Change simulation* (`PUT /api/v1/simulate-settings`, ADR-111 pattern); metrics.
  - *AC:* (1) a block rule for a name a device asked 40 times yesterday reports 40 newly blocked queries, 1 device, that name, and the rule as the deciding list; an allow rule for a name blocked yesterday reports it under newly allowed with the list that had blocked it; a group's upstream change reports the changed route counts; a change that affects nothing reports zeros. (2) Adding a list compiles **only** that list (test: the serving snapshot's version is unchanged and the side snapshot holds the new list's names only) and the merged decision equals a full compile's `decide` for a corpus of 10k names × 3 clients (property test over both lookup modes). (3) Bounds: a second simulation on the same node gets `409 simulation_busy`; `max_rows = 1000` on a 5,000-row log answers `partial: true` with exactly 1,000 rows read, newest first; a 5-s `max_secs` is honored within 1 s. (4) Privacy level 1 answers `unavailable` with the reason; a device-only change (assign a device to a group whose lists are the same) still works at level 1. (5) Federated: in the cluster e2e, a simulation on the replica includes the primary's rows and the controller's copy of a ship-mode node's rows, with `missingNodes` for a stopped node. (6) Determinism: two runs over the same log produce byte-identical `impact`. (7) `make bench-smoke` unchanged (the engine never touches the pipeline's state). (8) Playwright: the preview button on a quick block rule shows the count from real queries made in the test; Settings → System turns `plans_by_default` on (checked, applied, reverted); the MCP e2e shows a plan without `simulate` has no `impact`, one with `simulate = "24h"` has it, and with the toggle on every plan has it. (9) Docs (`running.md` *Trying a change against yesterday's traffic*), help topic, configuration reference, site monitoring and agents pages, `spec/06` §7.3.
  - *Done 2026-10-09:* `crates/wrendns/src/simulate.rs`: `Decider` (both configurations through the pipeline's own steps: `explain::answered_early`, quick rules and schedules at each row's time, `FilterState::list_rewrite`, the filter, AAAA filter, group rewrites and safe search, `Router::select`), the serving snapshot plus a side snapshot of only the changed lists (`changed_lists`, `compile_side` under `<data_dir>/snapshots/sim-*`, removed after) merged with `Matcher::decide_ranked` / `Ranked::{remap, merge}` in the candidate's list-ID space; `scan` over the query log newest first with `max_rows`/`max_secs`; `Tally` (bounded, mergeable, deterministic `finish`); one at a time per node (`409 simulation_busy`); `mode()` (disabled, privacy level, not applicable); `run_devices_only` at privacy level 1; RPC `sim.run` to every reachable peer with both shared parts, `missingNodes`; runs on its own background-priority thread. `server::build_candidate`. `simulate=`/`simulateUntil=` on every dry run (`wrendns_api::SimulateOpts`, carried through write forwarding with a longer deadline) adds `simulation`; `POST /api/v1/simulate`, `wrendns config simulate` / `wrendns ctl simulate`; MCP `simulate_change` and `simulate` on every `plan_*` tool (default `auto`; a busy node gives the plan with a `note`); `[simulate]` as a managed one-of (`ManagedKind::Simulate`, `/api/v1/simulate-settings/default`, scope `config:write:simulate`, Settings → System → Change simulation; no MCP tool); agents need `querylog:read`; metrics `wrendns_simulations_total{outcome}`, `wrendns_simulation_duration_seconds`, `wrendns_simulation_rows_total`. UI: `SimulationCard` on the quick-rule form, the device drawer, the config editor's preview (lists, groups, upstreams, schedules), and agents' plan cards. Help topic `simulate`; `running.md` *Trying a change against yesterday's traffic*; configuration reference; site monitoring and agents pages; `spec/06` §7.3. Tests: `obs_024_merged_decisions_equal_a_full_compile` (10k names × 3 clients × both lookups), `obs_024_a_block_rule_reports_what_it_would_have_blocked`, `…_an_allow_rule…`, `…_route_changes_and_no_op_changes`, `…_only_changed_lists_are_compiled`, `obs_024_bounds`, `obs_024_privacy_level_1`, `obs_024_deterministic_and_mergeable`, `obs_024_simulation_requests_over_http`, `obs_024_simulate_parameters`, `obs_024_simulation_routes_need_their_scope`; cluster e2e (the replica's simulation counts the primary's rows and its copy of the replica's shipped rows; the primary's, with the replica stopped, lists it in `missingNodes`); MCP e2e (no simulation without `simulate`, one with `"24h"`, refused without `querylog:read`, `simulate_change`, every plan with `plans_by_default`, agents can't change it); Playwright `obs_024 simulate a quick rule, and the simulation settings`. Bench-smoke unchanged (VM: cache-hot 571k q/s, miss-heavy p50 231 µs / p99 359 µs; the engine never touches the pipeline's state). ADR-115 amended (still Proposed): re-decide the configuration in effect rather than compare with the recorded status; `simulation`, not `impact` (taken); refused rows replayed; no `has_qlog` heartbeat bit; `auto`; level-1 device-only mode with `undetermined`; exact bounded counts instead of Space-Saving; scopes. Not done: pauses and CNAME-target blocks aren't replayed (by design, documented); a peer that can't fetch a changed list's file or URL is listed as missing.
- [x] **T13.2 Staged rollouts and pins.** *(CLU-013, CLU-003, CLU-008, OBS-010, ADR-116; design `docs/design/staged-rollouts.md`)* Two heads with targeted delivery; `[cluster.rollout]` (canaries — **empty by default, off until set** (owner 2026-10-09) —, bake_secs, guard thresholds, require_traffic, history) as a shared one-of section with Settings → Cluster → *Staged rollouts* (a canary picker over the cluster's nodes, sites, and "resolver pods"; `PUT /api/v1/cluster/rollout-settings`; GitOps shows the TOML); the guard from heartbeat serving stats, probes, readiness, and apply errors; promote/abort; pins as new versions with the diff; `versions.json` history with protected blobs; API, CLI, Cluster page (stage per node, bake countdown, guard readings, pin banner with diff, version list with Pin), MCP, alerts, health, metrics, events; Helm `cluster.rollout` values.
  - *AC:* (1) `deploy/cluster/rollout-e2e.sh` (CI): primary + canary replica + plain replica under two-server load; a record change reaches the canary within 5 s and the plain replica only after `bake_secs = 5`; the plain replica's applied version never equals the canary version before promotion. (2) A change that makes the canary SERVFAIL (an upstream group routed to a black hole for a test domain the load generator asks) is pinned back before the bake ends: the plain replica never applies it, the canary is back on the stable version within 5 s of the pin, 0 lost queries on either replica, `rollout_failed` fires once, health is `degraded` with `cluster_pinned`, and `PUT` of a record answers `409 cluster_pinned` with a non-empty diff. (3) `DELETE /api/v1/cluster/pin` resumes: the same change rolls out again and, with the black hole removed, promotes; `GET /api/v1/cluster/versions` lists both attempts with outcomes. (4) An operator `pin` of an older kept version applies on every node (the primary included) and the primary's own `explain` reflects it. (5) Failover during a pin: kill the primary, promote the eligible replica, it publishes still pinned (`pinned` in its first manifest). (6) N−1: `deploy/cluster/upgrade-e2e.sh` extended: the published edge binary as a replica receives only stable versions during a rollout. (7) Helm scaled e2e: with nothing set, a change reaches every pod at once (no rollout); after `PUT /cluster/rollout-settings { canaries: ["ephemeral"] }` the pods are canaries and `rollout_status` names them; an outside node that joins is non-canary. Playwright: Settings → Cluster picks a node as canary (checked, applied, reverted). (8) Unit: guard math (before/after shares, the 50-answer minimum, `require_traffic`), head selection per peer, `versions.json` rotation and blob protection, manifest `rollout`/`pinned` serialization defaults. (9) Promtool tests for the two alert rules in the chart. (10) Docs (`running.md` *Rolling a change out in stages*, *Pinning the cluster to a version*), help topics, configuration reference, site clusters page, `spec/12` §4.1.
  - *Done 2026-10-10:* `crates/wrendns/src/rollout.rs` (the version history `versions.json` with protected blobs, `rollout.json`, the guard over per-node heartbeat history: apply errors, not ready 15 s, listener checks, gone a minute after applying, and the SERVFAIL share against `max(before + 2, servfail_pct)` judged from 50 answers during the bake; (3) In the cluster e2e, a replica in maintenance that is then SIGSTOPped raises no `node_down` alert and the health level stays `healthy` with the node listed under `maintenance`; SIGCONT and ending maintenance restores normal evaluation (a later stop raises `node_down`). (4) A node in maintenance isn't elected: with auto failover and a witness, killing the primary while the only eligible replica is in maintenance elects nobody until maintenance ends (sim or e2e step). (4b) Handover: in the failover e2e, starting maintenance on the primary (auto mode, an eligible replica up) elects the replica within the lease window with 100 % of DNS answered and the old primary following; with `handover = false`, or in manual mode, the primary stays primary and the response carries `note: "promote another node first…"`. (5) `forSecs` > 86,400 and a missing reason are 422; an agent token asking for 3 h gets 422 with the 2 h cap in the hint. (6) The request on any node reaches the target node (e2e: start on the primary for the replica, the replica's file and readiness change); a target that's down answers 503. (8) Playwright: start maintenance from the Cluster page, see the banner and the health note, end it. ## M15 — Kubernetes workloads and failover drills (owner request 2026-10-18)
Two tasks from the design session of 2026-10-18, built in order T15.1 → T15.2 (independent; T15.2 gains from T15.1). Shared rules: nothing unpaid on the query path (A/B `make bench-smoke` and `bench.py sustain` on the build VM), DNS never depends on the Kubernetes API, a peer, or a report file (CLU-004), every new read federated with `missingNodes`, names at read time, privacy levels and exclusions, agent-ready APIs with MCP tools, no new `ui/` runtime dependency (both tasks under 25 KB gzipped), chart defaults unchanged for existing installs. Never touch the live nodes without the owner's go.

- [x] **T15.1 Kubernetes workloads as devices.** *(FLT-017, OBS-025, API-010, ADR-150; design `docs/design/kubernetes-workloads.md`)* A read-only pod/namespace watcher on the controller (no client crate), the `Workloads` table distributed to peers (`workloads.table`), `IdSource::Workload` in `ClientTable::identify`, groups from labels and `[[kubernetes.map]]`, a synthetic analytics key per workload, time-aware names at read time, `GET /api/v1/kubernetes/workloads` and `/status`, MCP `list_workloads` / `get_workload`, the Clients page's **Workloads** tab and chip glyph, chart values (`kubernetes.*`, `service.dns.clusterIP`), metrics, `kubernetes_stale` health, `WrenDNSKubernetesWatchStale`.

## M17 — Supportability (owner request 2026-11-15)

- [x] **T17.1 Support package.** *(OPS-011, API-003, AGT-001; GitHub issue #50)* A redacted diagnostics archive from the CLI, the API, and the System page: build and platform facts, the effective configuration without secrets, the cluster view and timeline, health checks, listener and upstream state, list counts, a metrics snapshot, aggregate statistics, recent logs (a `tracing` layer keeps a bounded in-memory ring and two rotating files of about 1 MiB under `<data_dir>/logs/`, since the process can't read its stderr back on any platform), and an opt-in query-log sample; three obfuscation levels (`strict` by default, then `standard` and `none`) with stable per-package pseudonyms; a manifest with per-category redaction counts. Design: ADR-156 (Accepted 2026-11-16).
  - *AC:* (1) a fixture with every kind of secret planted (password hashes, API, session, and join tokens, TOTP secret, OIDC secret, node and CA private keys, bootstrap secret, SMTP, webhook, and Git credentials) produces a package, in each level, that contains none of them (a scan for each planted value and for the PEM and token shapes); (2) at `strict` (the default), every planted IP, MAC, host, device, client, group, node, pod, namespace, e-mail, and home path is replaced, the same input always by the same pseudonym, two addresses of one /24 stay in one /24, private stays private, loopback, link-local, and the well-known public resolvers are unchanged, no query name appears anywhere, and only WARN and ERROR log lines are present; at `standard` INFO lines and the opt-in query-log sample appear with their names pseudonymized; at `none` real values are kept (the secrets are still gone), and the query-log sample is refused at `strict`; (3) `--reveal NAME` keeps that name and only it, `--keep-map` writes the map outside the package, and the API's map download works once, only for the package just made, only for an admin, and not after 10 minutes; (4) the manifest lists every file with its redaction counts and the level, and the counts match a recount of the fixture; (5) the CLI and the API produce the same package, `--list` writes nothing, a size over the cap is truncated and says so, and a slow or failing collector marks its file as missing instead of failing the package; (6) the redactor never panics and never leaves a planted value on arbitrary text (a fuzz target); (7) the log layer keeps the last 2,000 lines in memory and two rotating files of about 1 MiB under `<data_dir>/logs/`, lines from before a restart reach the package, a full channel drops and counts instead of blocking, and a read-only data directory falls back to memory; (8) the bug-report issue form asks for it, and `docs/running.md`, the site, and OpenAPI are done (it is not an MCP tool).
  - *Decided (owner, 2026-11-15):* default level `strict`, with fuller logs and the query-log sample opt-in; the query-log sample is offered; no MCP tool for now; the UI offers the pseudonym map as a short-lived second download (in memory, gone after the first download or 10 minutes); the log files default to on (`[support] persist_logs`).
  - *Progress 2026-11-16:* phase 1 done: `support_log` (a `tracing` layer: a ring of 2,000 INFO+ lines from the first line on, two rotating files of about 1 MiB under `<data_dir>/logs/` once the data directory is locked, lines of the last run read back at start, a bounded channel that drops and counts, a read-only directory leaving the ring, flushed at shutdown) and `[support] persist_logs`, node-local and restart-only; the console keeps following `WRENDNS_LOG`. AC (7) is covered. Next: the archive writer, redaction, pseudonyms, and the classification table; then the collectors and the three surfaces.
  - *Progress 2026-11-16 (phase 2):* the pure core is the new `wrendns-support` crate: a ustar and gzip writer (`archive`), keyed pseudonyms with Crypto-PAn style address permutation that keeps subnets, private ranges, public-ness, loopback, link-local and the well-known resolvers (`pseudo`), the two-pass redactor (`redact`: one multi-pattern search for known names and inline secrets, then shape scanners for addresses, MACs, e-mail, URLs, host names, home paths, PEM blocks and token-looking runs; nothing is scanned twice), configuration classification that fails closed (`classify`: a class table for every string field of the generated schema, numbers, flags and fixed words plain by type, an unclassified field dropped and listed, credential-looking key names dropped as a second net, and tests that fail when a schema field has no class or a table entry matches no field), the manifest and the package builder with the size cap (`manifest`, `package`), and the fuzz target `support_redact` in the nightly workflow. AC (1), (2), (4), part of (5) and (6) are covered at the library level. Next: the collectors, the CLI, the API and the System page.

## M40 — Unbound parity for the recursive resolver (owner request, fork #114)

The gap audit of fork #114 is `docs/design/unbound-parity.md`: Unbound's features by area, what WrenDNS does today with the file that shows it, the gap size, and build, parity, already better or will not do, with the reason. The tasks below are the items it marks "build", in its order; everything it marks "will not do" is recorded there with the reason. Requirement IDs reserved for these tasks (free on 2026-11-25; recheck when the rows are written, and add each row to `spec/01` when its task starts): **DNS-902** recursor hardening, **DNS-903** infrastructure cache and fallbacks, **DNS-904** recursor observability and lookup trace, **DNS-905** cache and recursor controls, **DNS-906** RFC 5011 rollover, **DNS-907** aggressive NSEC3, **DNS-908** cookies, padding and keepalive, **DNS-909** local root zone, **DNS-910** special-name parity, **FLT-906** RPZ as a list source, **API-903** the `unbound.conf` importer. Each task writes its ADR at its start. Every task adds its UI control, help topic and Playwright test for each setting, route or tool (API-901); every task that touches the recursor tests against a local authoritative fixture (`crates/wrendns-recursor/tests/recursor.rs`), and every task on the query path runs `make bench-smoke` (AGENTS rule 4).

- [ ] **T40.1 Recursor hardening.** *(reserved DNS-902; DNS-012, DNS-015, API-901)* No queries to loopback, unspecified or link-local server addresses, and private ranges only inside stub zones unless allowed (Unbound's `do-not-query-localhost`); lame answers counted as failures for the server, so a fast lame server stops coming first; the task's ADR decides whether a minimised query answered with a DNSSEC-proven NXDOMAIN stops the walk (RFC 8020, as Unbound's `harden-below-nxdomain`) and how the validator's result reaches the recursor, while an unsigned NXDOMAIN, even with AA and SOA, keeps the full-name fallback of ADR-074 because some servers answer NXDOMAIN for empty non-terminals; NSEC3 iteration limits set per RFC 9276; `ecs` refused on a `recursive://` upstream; UI fields on the Upstreams page for `qname_minimization`, `case_randomization`, `ipv6` (which have none today) and the new settings.
  - *AC:* (1) a fixture zone delegating to `127.0.0.1` and `::1` gets no query sent there and answers SERVFAIL with an EDE, while a stub zone whose servers are private addresses still resolves; (2) a fixture with a lame first server (fast, REFUSED) and a good second one: after the first lookup the good server is asked first; (3) a fixture that answers NXDOMAIN, unsigned with AA and SOA, for an empty non-terminal still resolves a name below it (the full name is asked), and if the ADR adopts stopping, a signed fixture whose NXDOMAIN validates sends no full-name query; (4) an NSEC3 denial above the chosen iteration limit validates as insecure, as the ADR records; (5) `ecs` on `recursive://` fails validation with the field named; (6) Playwright: the recursive options are shown and saved for a `recursive://` upstream and hidden for others; (7) `make bench-smoke` within budget.

RFC 8020 (Unbound's `harden-below-nxdomain`): when a minimised query is answered with an NXDOMAIN that DNSSEC proves, nothing exists below that name and the walk stops, instead of asking the full name as today. The task needs its own decision record, because the recursor sits below validation and cannot tell a proven NXDOMAIN from an unsigned one: the record chooses how the validator's result reaches it (a proven-NXDOMAIN verdict per minimised name, or a check above the recursor as a second validated step) and what happens when validation is off. An unsigned NXDOMAIN, even with AA and SOA, keeps the full-name fallback of ADR-074.

The dnstap writer is started once, so the task states in its decision record whether a change applies on reload or needs a restart (today the file's own rule is "restart after changing it"), and the card says which, with a restart prompt if needed. It is the owner's decision that this is its own task and not a read-only card; the mechanism is the task's to design.

## M39 — CI speed (owner request 2026-11-20)

The owner asked for faster CI, and speed is a goal of the CI redesign (owner decision, 2026-11-19). The decided target is six workflows: `pr.yml` (under 15 minutes), `main.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `release.yml`, `site.yml` and CodeQL, with `pr-ok` as the single required check (ADR-1073). The tasks below are spec only. Each one is measured with `scripts/ci_bench.py` (T39.12) before and after it lands, and none is ticked until its acceptance criteria pass in CI.

- [ ] **T39.1 CI tiers, changes job and pr-ok.** *(OPS-004, NFR-005; ADR-1073)* Split CI into the six-workflow shape: a `changes` job, a fast tier on pull requests, a full tier on main (also on `ci:full` and dispatch), a nightly tier, and one `pr-ok` job that is the only required check. `upstream-watch` is deleted and the `feat/ipam-integrations` triggers are dropped.
  - *AC:* (1) a docs-only pull request skips every heavy job and `pr-ok` passes; (2) an injected failure in any needed job, and a job skipped after a failed dependency, each make `pr-ok` fail; (3) a push to main that touches `crates/wrendns-cluster` runs cluster3; (4) nightly runs cluster3 and keepalived on its schedule (proved by a dispatch run); (5) the fast tier takes 10 minutes or less and `pr.yml` under 15 minutes, warm, as the median of three runs.

## M38 — The network map: Wiring, Places, device pages and live motion (owner request 2026-11-19)

**Owner decisions (2026-11-19), final:** (1) first among the enhancements, after the speed wave, as one big development wave that starts once the repository is public (so GitHub Actions minutes cost nothing), with #110's location names and T24.45's per-node certificate expiries folded in where they share pages; (2) all four parts in the first release; (3) the motion shows real data: dot speed and density from per-link traffic and DNS query rates, blocked queries in red; (4) Places shows devices that are not on the IP network (Zigbee, Z-Wave, Thread and Matter) from Home Assistant, read-only, through their hub. ADR-1071.

The owner's network-map idea, sharpened by a look at the public netpulse demo (AGPL-3.0: its rendered pages only, as ideas; none of its code, markup or assets, ADR-1033 and the clean-room rule): a physical **Wiring** view, a **Places** view by site, floor and area, a detail page per device, and clients-list upgrades, with motion that means something.

- [ ] **T38.1 Design.** *(requirement IDs reserved here; ADR-1071)* `docs/design/network-map.md`: the graph model (nodes, links, places, sources and confidence), the deterministic layout and pins, the motion vocabulary and its data, the size plan (a lazy chunk, no graph or animation library), accessibility (the links table as the text equivalent, `prefers-reduced-motion`, motion paused in a hidden tab), and the split into tracks.
- [ ] **T38.2 The topology graph API and MCP tool.** *(AGT-001..005)* `GET /api/v1/topology` from the CMDB and the integrations: nodes (gateway, switches, access points, WrenDNS nodes, hypervisors with their guests, clients, VPN peers, inferred switches for ports holding several MACs), links (cable, Wi-Fi uplink, client Wi-Fi by band, tunnel; speed, port, LLDP, signal, status) and places; per-link rates for the motion; manual overrides (a device's kind, a link's medium); an MCP tool to read it.
  - *AC:* (1) the demo network gives a golden graph; (2) a port with three MACs and no LLDP neighbour yields one inferred switch; (3) an override survives a re-read of the source.
- [ ] **T38.3 The Wiring view.** Hand-written SVG in a lazy chunk: the gateway at the centre, access points and switches around it, clients fanned per port or radio with a "+N" overflow, guests in a grid under their hypervisor, VPN peers on their own row; a deterministic layout (the same data gives the same picture), drag to pin with pins saved per user, zoom, pan and reset, labels on links ("Cable 1G · LLDP"), a legend, and the links table under the map (link, type, speed, latency, signal, status).
  - *AC:* (1) two loads of the same data draw the same positions (screenshot test); (2) a pinned node stays put after a refresh; (3) every link on the map is a row in the table, reachable by keyboard; (4) the UI budget holds (the chunk is not loaded until the view opens).
- [ ] **T38.4 Motion from real data.** Dots along each live link whose speed and density follow the link's measured rate (quantised, capped), DNS queries as dots into the serving WrenDNS node with blocked ones turning red and stopping there, a soft pulse on status dots, a slow halo on the gateway, links drawn in on load; off under `prefers-reduced-motion`, paused while the tab is hidden, and a "motion" toggle.
  - *AC:* (1) a link with no traffic shows no dots; (2) a tenfold rate change visibly changes the dot rate within one refresh; (3) reduced motion shows a static map with the same information; (4) a hidden tab uses no animation frames (measured).
- [ ] **T38.5 Places.** Site > floor > area from Home Assistant's floor and area registries (the area is already read with each device's name) and from #110's location names; devices grouped by area, each marked with how it connects; floor and area as filters on the clients list and the map.
  - *AC:* (1) a device given an area in Home Assistant appears in that area within one read; (2) a device with no area is listed under "No area", not hidden.
- [ ] **T38.6 Non-IP devices through their hub.** *(read-only)* Home Assistant's device list for Zigbee, Z-Wave, Thread and Matter devices, shown in Places linked to their coordinator or border router, never in the DNS clients list or the query log; no write to Home Assistant.
  - *AC:* (1) a Zigbee device from the test Home Assistant shows under its area, linked to the coordinator; (2) it does not appear in `/api/v1/clients`.
- [ ] **T38.7 Device detail pages.** One page per device (UniFi devices and WrenDNS nodes): a health score, performance (CPU, memory, temperature with now and peak), an information list (uptime, last reboot and why, model, firmware, "open web UI"), a facts strip, the port strip (an RJ45 per port with its link light, what is plugged in, speed, WAN set apart) from the UniFi port table, Wi-Fi radio cards (channel, width, power, clients, a congestion tag), on a WrenDNS node a DNS card (queries, blocked, % blocked, average answer time, hourly bars, top blocked names, active lists, protected clients) and its certificate expiry (T24.45), and its connected clients.
  - *AC:* (1) every port the UniFi read reports is drawn with the right state; (2) the DNS card's figures match the dashboard's for the same node and window.
- [ ] **T38.8 Clients list upgrades.** Summary tiles (online, new in 7 days, weak signal, protected, roaming in 24 h), the "via" column (which device a client connects through), floor and area filters, a column picker and CSV export.
- [ ] **T38.9 Closing.** docs/running.md "The network map", the help pages, the site's tour screenshots, the README fork block, and e2e specs for the views.

## M37 — Shadow AI detection (owner request 2026-11-19) [cloud #4]

**Owner decisions (2026-11-19), final:** (1) the catalog is in-house, from vendor documentation; (2) Shadow AI is **commercial-only and hosted-only** in WrenDNS Cloud, computed from a small generic node export, with enforcement returned as ordinary group policy, amending ADR-1052 §3 for the evidence the cloud keeps; (3) off until an admin turns it on and acknowledges a monitoring notice, then every group at Monitor; (4) full per-device findings at privacy level 1, matched before hashing, after an extra acknowledgement, and off at level 2 and above; (5) the use rule (2 active 5-minute periods or 2 days, merged evidence or agent confirmation, "OS assistant present", the ambient lab before the first release, the owner's own devices only with a go-ahead); (6) vendor-stated, dated, linked facts; (7) approved tenants only where hostnames split; (8) an alert on every first use per device, quiet for the first day, first-seen kept by the cloud, grouped and rate limited; (9) minors the operator's responsibility; (10) no Warn in v1 (Off, Allow, Monitor, Block). ADR-1055 to ADR-1059 Accepted with these decisions; ADR-1060 (the node side) Accepted. **Owner decisions on cloud writes (2026-11-19), final (decision D):** Shadow AI Block and Allow become ordinary signed policy changes (M36's ADR-1061 and ADR-1063), replacing the subscribed `ai-block-<group>` and `ai-allow-<group>` lists; the catalog's class map arrives over the platform channel signed by the content key (ADR-1062); ADR-1060 amended accordingly.

Find, report and govern AI service use per device and group (cloud #4), as a paid WrenDNS Cloud feature. Design: `docs/design/shadow-ai.md`; ADR-1055 (the catalog, in the service), ADR-1056 (detection and the alert, in the service), ADR-1057 (policy modes and the group lists), ADR-1058 (privacy defaults; amends ADR-102 for the export), ADR-1059 (hosted-only: boundary, cloud data and retention, latency, offline, tiers; amends ADR-1052 §3 and ADR-1047 point 8), ADR-1060 (the node's generic export, and class rules over a content-signed class map with Block and Allow as signed changes; Accepted and amended 2026-11-19). The rules that do not bend: DNS never depends on the cloud (class rules keep working on the last good class map, which freezes, never empties, on cancellation); the cloud never makes a Block or Allow on its own (each is signed by an editor); no Shadow AI logic or catalog in the open node; nothing on the query path; only names in the tenant's class map leave the node, as numbers; every page says what DNS cannot see; no prompts, content or filenames ever. Phases: 0 = the node (AGPL), T37.2 and T37.3, after M36's T36.4 and T36.5 (and, for T37.3, T36.15, T36.16 and T36.18); 1 = the service, T37.4 to T37.10, after M36's T36.9 (the portal), the owner's tenant first; 2 = sale, T37.11, with M36's phase 2 (billing, privacy policy, DPA); later = T37.12 to T37.15. Node tasks ship their UI, help topic and Playwright test, run `make bench-smoke` when they touch `wrendns-filter` or `wrendns-telemetry`, and report RSS (ADR-1031) and image (ADR-916) deltas; service tasks are built in the service's repository (ADR-1052 §2) with the portal UI, help topic and browser tests in the same task.

Review fixes 2026-11-19. Revised the same day for the owner's decisions: hosted-only architecture (what the node sends and the privacy level's effect, the cloud data model and retention amending ADR-1052 §3, latency, offline behaviour, tiers), the catalog subscription and delayed-open packaging removed, Warn moved to a later phase, the first-use alert with grouping and rate limits, ADR-1055 to ADR-1059 Accepted and ADR-1060 added as Proposed. ## M36 — WrenDNS Cloud: hosted control plane, roaming resolver, configure-once names (owner idea 2026-11-19) [cloud #3]

**Owner decisions (2026-11-19): all ten recommendations accepted** (the list in `docs/design/hosted.md`, "Owner decisions"). The tenant-name domain is **wrendns.net** (`<slug>.wrendns.net`, device and dynamic names on `<slug>-dev.wrendns.net`; to register for at least two years and submit to the Public Suffix List; the portal stays `dns.wrendns.com`).

**Owner decisions on cloud writes (2026-11-19), final** (owner request: "The cloud control plane needs to be able to update the connected home nodes. Cloud based filtering needs to be in sync with what is on-prem and vice-versa"; full text in `docs/design/hosted.md`, "Owner decisions on cloud writes"): **A** two trusted channels: (1) the user channel, with portal sign-in through Microsoft Entra External ID and every cloud-originated change to everyday policy signed by the editor's change-signing passkey enrolled on the node at home, verified, checked against the user's node role, applied and audited on the node, the editor's signature alone as approval, guarded settings home-only or custom-domain-only; (2) the platform channel, machine to machine, with the release key and a new content key under offline roots, delivering only signed content and opted-in actions and never changing user policy; **B** two-way sync with home preferred (per-entry versions, a fast path at the base, automatic merges, home wins a same-entry conflict parked in the portal, Pending, Applied and Accepted, on-prem edits flowing up at once to a cloud that subscribes like a replica without being a member); **C** the cloud resolver in the MVP (T36.12 moved in; no more "fails closed when home is down"; queued signed edits with expiry while home is offline and "apply to roaming now"); **D** Shadow AI Block and Allow as ordinary signed policy changes (M37). ADR-1047 and ADR-1049 to ADR-1052 amended; ADR-1061 to ADR-1066 Proposed (their open details are listed in hosted.md for the owner).

**Owner decisions needed first** (asked together at the start, with "accept all recommendations"; the full list with options is at the end of `docs/design/hosted.md`): the domain for tenant names and the slug rules (a dedicated PSL-listed suffix with a `<slug>-dev` site for device names, `dns.wrendns.com` as the portal); SNI passthrough to each node's own UI or a cloud proxy; sign-in over the relay (a node-local table, pending by default, a node-held passkey or TOTP on every relayed sign-in, `max_role` operator); admin and guarded work from away and remote MCP (off over hosted names by default); leaving the service (the free home keep-alive, then DNS-PERSIST-01); roaming when home is down (fail closed in v1, stated in the tier); where the broker runs and DDoS protection (two VMs behind a floating edge address); the open-core boundary and the service's licence; tiers and prices; data residency and the cloud's data.

A hosted service run by MySummitKeep, LLC through which a tenant reaches their own nodes' UI from anywhere, gets a public name and a roaming DoH/DoT resolver, and sets each device up once for home and away (cloud #3). It absorbs cloud #2's location-scoped names, managed names, dynamic DNS and DNS-provider integrations. Design: `docs/design/hosted.md`; ADR-1047 (the tunnel and SNI passthrough), ADR-1048 (node cloud identity and enrolment; the cloud is never a cluster member), ADR-1049 (authorization on the node, custom roles with create, update and remove), ADR-1050 (names, split horizon and the roaming path), ADR-1051 (certificates), ADR-1052 (open core, data handling, platform), all Accepted 2026-11-19 and amended the same day per the owner decisions on cloud writes; ADR-1061 (change signing), ADR-1062 (the platform channel and its keys), ADR-1063 (two-way sync and conflicts; amends ADR-054 for cloud-origin changes), ADR-1064 (the cloud resolver in the MVP), ADR-1065 (Entra External ID), ADR-1066 (opt-in managed updates; amends ADR-046), Proposed; ADR-1067 (enterprise connections, the portal-minted subject, verified domains; amends ADR-1065), ADR-1068 (the SCIM server), ADR-1069 (JIT and SCIM, node group rules, deprovisioning, onboarding; amends ADR-1049 and ADR-1061) and ADR-1070 (Business packaging; amends ADR-1052), Proposed 2026-11-19 for the owner's cloud-identity requirement. **M32 is merged into M36:** its research stays under M32 and its tasks are carried here (T32.1 by T36.2, T32.5 by T36.7 and T36.10, T32.6 and T32.7 by T36.8, T32.2, T32.3, T32.4 and T32.8 by T36.12, T32.9 by T36.14). The rule that does not bend: DNS never depends on the cloud (AGENTS rule 5, CLU-004); a device at home never touches it, and cancelling never breaks DNS at home (the home keep-alive, ADR-1051). Phases: 0 = T36.2, T36.3, T36.10 (node only, AGPL); 1 = the MVP, T36.4 to T36.9, T36.12 and T36.15 to T36.20 (the owner's own tenant); 2 = beta, T36.13 (the PSL, Let's Encrypt rate-limit and Azure DNS record-set requests filed first) and the portal's member, abuse, billing, custom-name and DDoS work; 3 = paid tiers, T36.11 and Business identity, T36.21 to T36.26; after general availability, T36.27. Requirement IDs reserved for the new tasks (free on 2026-11-19; recheck when the rows are written): **CLD-910** change signing, **CLD-911** two-way sync, **CLD-912** the platform channel, **CLD-913** managed updates, **CLD-914** portal identity, **CLD-915** enterprise SSO (connections, domains, home-realm discovery), **CLD-916** SCIM provisioning, **CLD-917** node group rules and deprovisioning.

## M34 — Public authoritative DNS, like BIND (owner request 2026-11-19) [fork #30]

Serve the owner's own domains to the internet: primary and secondary zones, transfers with TSIG, NOTIFY, DNSSEC signing, dynamic updates, rate limiting, views, catalog zones, and a cluster in which every member serves. This reverses `spec/00` §3's non-goal ("use a real authoritative server for public zones"), so the first task records that in an ADR. **The rule that does not bend:** a public authoritative listener never recurses, caches, filters or logs the public internet by default; a node refuses to start if a public-facing listener would also recurse. Full scope and the owner decisions are in fork #30; they are asked together at the start, with "accept all recommendations".

- [ ] **T34.1 Design.** *(new DNS-9xx requirements; ADR reversing the spec/00 §3 non-goal)* The authoritative engine kept off the resolver hot path (its own listeners, a compiled zone index swapped atomically), zone sources (files, API/UI), transfers (AXFR/IXFR, TSIG, NOTIFY, secondaries, hidden primary), DNSSEC signing and key rollover, RFC 2136 updates, RRL and abuse limits, views, catalog zones, cluster replication of zones and keys, BIND `named.conf` import, observability, API/MCP, the performance gate (against NSD/Knot/BIND) and the test plan. Then refine T34.2 onwards into numbered steps with acceptance criteria.
- [ ] **T34.2 onwards.** Defined by T34.1.

## M33 — Independence: the fork's own name (owner decision 2026-11-19, ADR-1026)

The fork goes its own way (ADR-1026). Before anything is published outside the development network it takes its own name: WrenDNS (owner, 2026-11-19).

- [x] **T33.1 Leave upstream's fork network.** *(ADR-1026)* Export every issue, comment and label (`.github/issues-archive/`), the owner clicks Leave fork network, then recreate the issues in order so #1 to #29 keep their numbers. *Done 2026-11-19: exported (29 issues, 27 comments, 12 labels) and the owner left the fork network. GitHub kept every issue, comment, label and the pin on #18, so nothing was recreated; the archive stays as a backup. Removed from the tree on 2026-11-25 by owner decision; the owner keeps a copy.*
- [x] **T33.2 A new name: WrenDNS.** *(ADR-1026)* **Owner decisions 2026-11-19:** the name is **WrenDNS**, with a public website on **wrendns.com** (a web search found no other product of that name). The rename covers everything, **crates included** (`telltale-*` to `wrendns-*`, the binary `telltale` to `wrendns`; owner: "rebrand the software from telltale to wrendns"), and runs on a clean main after the open branches are merged. Metrics: both `telltale_*` and `wrendns_*` are exported for one release, the bundled Grafana dashboards move to `wrendns_*`, then `telltale_*` is dropped. The GitHub repository is renamed to `nbacheller/wrendns` when the rename merges (GitHub redirects the old URLs). Old paths, environment variables and the `telltale` command keep working for one release with a warning. The site moves to wrendns.com. **Functional links move too, not only text (found 2026-11-19):** the update check and self-update read `https://github.com/paimonsoror/telltaledns/releases` (`crates/telltale/src/updates.rs:17`, `selfupdate.rs:20`) and verify with upstream's release key (`deploy/release/telltale-release.pub`); with `[updates] check` on by default, a WrenDNS node would report upstream's builds as updates.
