Checks: `npm run check`, `npm run build`, the whole Playwright suite in order (346 passed, 2 skipped; a later run on a loaded host failed `flt_901` in `9-categories.spec.ts`, which passes alone and in the first full run), `cargo test -p wrendns` (the palette changed; `dsc_906_write_volume_of_a_stable_network` exits the run with the in-process watchdog's 70 when it runs beside the rest on this loaded host and passes alone, as T33.2 notes), `cargo clippy -p wrendns --all-targets`, `site/build.py --check`, `spec/trace.py --check`. Before and after screenshots of 47 views in Day and Night (94 each) on the demo network are in `.wt/brand-shots/` for the owner's review (not committed); the demo network no longer sets group colours, so its groups show the flock. *Deferred:* the API's doc comments and OpenAPI still say "Names on my network" (Rust, `wrendns-api`); the CMDB names a listener "Udp 127.0.0.1:…" (the server's own label); about 300 off-scale paddings in the pages beyond the primitives; the device timeline's 9px "new" mark.

## M32 — Cloud-hosted resolver and roaming-device clients (owner request 2026-11-18) [cloud #1] — merged into M36

**Merged into M36 (2026-11-19, cloud #3).** The research below stays as written. The tasks are carried by M36: T32.1 by T36.2, T32.5 by T36.7 and T36.10, T32.6 and T32.7 by T36.8, T32.2, T32.3, T32.4 and T32.8 by T36.12, T32.9 by T36.14. Work is tracked there, not here. ADR-1048 replaces T32.8's option of the cloud node joining the home cluster (a cluster member can vouch for any user's role, ADR-054).

A WrenDNS that devices use when they're away from home, hosted on a free or nearly free Azure tier, with native DoH or DoT setup for Windows, macOS, iOS and Android, and the same per-device policy at home and away. Research (2026-11-18, in cloud #1) found:
- **Azure:**
  - Container Apps serves DoH on 443 with a free managed certificate. One always-on replica costs about $4–14 a month above the free grant, or it's free if it scales to zero, with a 10–30 s cold start.
  - DoT and UDP 53 are not available there without a paid VNet environment, about $25 a month.
  - The free-account VMs serve every protocol, but only for 12 months.
- **Clients:** Windows 11, macOS 11+ and iOS 14+ take a DoH template with a per-device path. Android's built-in Private DNS is DoT only, by hostname. Windows 10 has no native DoH.

**Owner decisions needed first** (asked together at the start, with "accept all recommendations"): hosting (Container Apps, the 12-month VM, or both templates); Android (DoT or an app); client apps (build or document permissive third-party ones); the domain and the DNS provider for DNS-01; how the cloud node shares the home policy (cluster member or Git); the query log's retention and location in the cloud.

- [ ] **T32.1 A public listener is never an open resolver.** *(Moved to T36.2.)* *(new DNS-901; spec/08 §6; ADR)*
  - **Known-ID gate:** a per-listener `require_client_id` setting. Queries are refused (REFUSED + EDE) unless the DoH path or SNI carries a known device ID or token. The check runs off the allocation-free path, in the same place as `allowed_networks`; bench-smoke.
  - **Unknown IDs:** refused without saying whether the ID exists, and rate limited per address and per ID.
  - **Startup warning:** the missing check from spec/08:114 (a listener bound to a public IP without the gate).
  - **Ships with:** UI on the listener settings, a help topic, and Playwright.
- [ ] **T32.2 A stateless cloud profile.** *(Moved to T36.12.)* *(new OPS-902; ADR)*
  - **Storage:** runs on ephemeral storage, so SQLite never sits on SMB or NFS (Azure Files). Startup warns when the data dir is a network file system.
  - **Config:** from Git (the existing Git source) or the home cluster (T32.8).
  - **Query log:** kept locally with a short retention, or sent to a sink.
  - **Startup and size:** cold start measured in a 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GiB container; the RSS budgets hold.
- [ ] **T32.3 Azure Container Apps template.** *(Moved to T36.12.)* After T32.1–T32.2.
  - **Template:** Bicep (plus `azd`), with the image from GHCR, DoH on 443, a custom domain and a managed certificate.
  - **Scaling and probes:** the min-replicas choice with its cost table (free with scale to zero, or about $4–14 a month always on); `/readyz` probes.
  - **Deploy check:** a test that the deploy works (what-if or a throwaway resource group, documented); docs with a cost and limits table.
- [ ] **T32.4 Azure VM template (free-account B1s/B2pts v2, 12 months).** *(Moved to T36.12.)*
  - **Setup:** cloud-init with the native systemd install, serving DoH, DoT and DoQ (UDP 53 off by default), with the firewall rules and unattended upgrades.
  - **Docs:** the 12-month limit and what it costs after, the static-IP cost, and the egress allowance (100 GB a month free).
- [ ] **T32.5 Certificates.** *(Moved to T36.7 and T36.10.)* Decide in an ADR: built-in ACME, a vetted permissive crate (cargo-deny, image delta) or a certbot sidecar. The wildcard certificate for SNI device IDs needs DNS-01, so pick the provider APIs. The certificate hot-reload exists already.
- [ ] **T32.6 Device onboarding.** *(Moved to T36.8.)* Per-device tokens: create, rotate and revoke, audited, and agent-safe (plan-only for agents). An "Add a device away from home" page generates the setup:
  - **Apple:** a `.mobileconfig` (DoH ServerURL with the path token, or DoT ServerName, with OnDemand rules for home Wi-Fi), plus the declarative `com.apple.configuration.network.dns-settings` for OS 27. Optional signing.
  - **Windows 11:** a PowerShell/`netsh` script, and Group Policy/Intune notes.
  - **Android:** the Private DNS hostname (DoT) and Chrome's Secure DNS template.
  - **Delivery:** a QR code. A setup link expires and is single use. API, MCP and help topics; Playwright.
- [ ] **T32.7 Client apps (decision first).** *(Moved to T36.8.)* Either document permissive third-party clients (Rethink DNS, Apache-2.0, for Android DoH; dnscrypt-proxy, ISC, for Windows 10) and generate their configs in T32.6, or build our own apps (VpnService on Android with the Play declaration; NEDNSSettingsManager on Apple with the dns-settings entitlement). Record the choice in an ADR.
- [ ] **T32.8 One policy at home and away.** *(Moved to T36.12.)* A device keeps its identity and group on both resolvers (`id:<device>` matches at home and in the cloud). The cloud node either joins the home cluster (which link direction, given NAT, and secrets handover) or shares its config through Git; ADR. The device policy panel (T24.30) shows which resolver a device is using.
- [ ] **T32.9 Closing.** *(Moved to T36.14.)*
  - **Docs:** docs/running.md "Away from home", the site page, and the README fork block.
  - **Tests:** an e2e with a fake public listener (the gate refuses an unknown ID, a known ID resolves); an image size check.
  - **Live check:** real devices on the cloud instance, only with the owner's go-ahead.

## M31 — CMDB: configuration items from many sources (owner request 2026-11-18) [fork #21]

One configuration item (CI) per real thing on the network, built from every source that reports on it: UniFi, Home Assistant, SNMP, imported scans, Pi-hole imports, DHCP leases, query attribution and Kubernetes. Each source's record is kept and linked to its CI, the owner declares the definitive source per attribute, and changes go through a MACD lifecycle (move, add, change, delete). It builds on M25's inventory (T25.1, keyed by MAC, ADR-910) and keeps M25's rules: read-only towards devices, off the DNS path, bounded storage, privacy levels respected, one management plane in a cluster. The standing rule applies: every setting and action ships with a UI control, a help topic and a Playwright test.

- [x] **T31.1 Design.** *(new DSC-9xx requirements; ADR)* Design only. The CI types and relations (device, interface, network/VLAN, WrenDNS node, service, upstream; on network, attached to port, member of group); the source record (as reported, first and last seen, source and its identity); reconciliation (match keys in order: MAC, serial, router client ID, hostname plus network; manual link and unlink; how M25's MAC merge becomes the first rule); the definitive-source model (a precedence per CI type and attribute, a per-CI override, manual values as a source, a conflict view where a source disagrees with the definitive value, what happens when the definitive source goes silent); MACD (the change record and its states requested, approved, done and rejected; who may approve; changes detected from sources, such as a new device, a moved port or a disappeared device, raised as a MACD to confirm; history and audit); storage and retention, the API and MCP tools (read for agents, writes plan-only), federation in a cluster, and the test plan. Batch the owner decisions it needs into one AskUserQuestion at the milestone start. Then refine T31.2 to T31.6 into numbered steps with acceptance criteria. *Done 2026-11-18 (track cmdb-design; revised after review the same day: aligned with ADR-998/999, device and interface levels resolved separately, port keys, per-source detection with an acknowledged value, caps, write volume, backups, named-node failover): `docs/design/cmdb.md`, ADR-1004 (model, reconciliation, definitive sources, MACD) and ADR-1005 (storage, API, MCP, federation, retention), both Proposed; requirements DSC-901 to DSC-907. Consistent with T24.29 (a profile is a group; `member_of`), T24.30 (the CI page's Policy panel calls its endpoint), T25.18 (ADR-998, ADR-999: the `[[group_link]]` keeps its direction `unifi_definitive`, `wrendns_definitive` or `two_way`; the CMDB mirrors it read-only, `member_of` is a set with the sources `config` and `unifi:<router>`, and CMDB precedence never drives the sync, which amends ADR-998 §14) and M25 (T25.1's merge is rule R2; ADR-910's orders are the default precedence; T25.6's rows are the `snmp` source). The owner decisions for the milestone are the 16 questions at the end of `docs/design/cmdb.md`, asked together at the start of T31.2 with an accept-all option; ADR-1004 and ADR-1005 move to Accepted on the owner's word. Deferred: none.*
- [x] **T31.2 CIs, source records and reconciliation.** *(DSC-901, DSC-902, DSC-903, DSC-906; ADR-1004, ADR-1005)* After T31.1 and the owner's answers. The store, the ingestion from each existing source, matching, and the manual link, unlink, merge and split in the UI.
  1. **Spike (first).** Confirm the ADR-917 replication code takes a non-secret writer (the authored tables); if not, record the fallback amendment of ADR-1005 §6 before building on it.
  2. `[cmdb]` settings kind (admin-only, managed, schema, OpenAPI), the designation gate shared with `[discovery]`, the privacy validation (level 2 and above), a settings panel, help topic `cmdb`, and a Playwright test.
  3. `wrendns-store` migration and the store: CI registry (with `first_seen`, CI-level `last_seen`, `days_seen`), source records, links and pins, aliases, port aliases; the compact in-memory index; caps, CI-cap eviction and retention (ADR-1005 §3, §5); batched `last_seen` flushes and write-on-change; its own thread.
  4. The source sink and bounded channel, and one adapter per source: routers (UniFi, OPNsense, Home Assistant), neighbour table, SNMP, imports, leases, mDNS, `queries` (a once-a-minute read of the aggregator's snapshot), Kubernetes (when on), `config` and `cluster`. (No Pi-hole importer source: owner question 14, 2026-11-19.)
  5. The reconciliation engine, rules R1 to R5 resolved separately for the interface level and the device level (a disagreement raises a merge proposal), port CIs keyed by (device CI, normalised port id) with the SNMP, UniFi and LLDP normalisers and the alias table, merge, split and alias redirect; M25's MAC merge shares its normalisation code. R4 uses only keys that survive a MAC change (Home Assistant device id, SNMP chassis id, UniFi infrastructure device id) and never a UniFi client `_id`.
  6. Link, unlink, merge and split API (dry run, idempotency, reason, audit) and the UI controls with a preview of the records that would move.
  7. Metrics (`wrendns_cmdb_*`), the status API, health reasons that never mark DNS unhealthy.
  - *AC:* (1) each rule links, and an ambiguous record stays unlinked with a proposal (`dsc_903_*`); (2) unlink pins and survives the next batch; merge leaves a redirecting alias; (3) reconciling the same batches in any order gives the same links (property test); (4) a Home Assistant device with two MACs, or an SNMP chassis seen under a new MAC, links to one device CI with a new interface CI under it, an interface is never moved to another MAC, and a UniFi client `_id` is never used as a key (`dsc_903_*`); a record whose MAC and serial point at different devices links nothing at device level and raises a merge proposal; a switch port seen by SNMP `ifName` and UniFi `port_idx` is one port CI once aliased and an unaliased one is `unmapped_port`, never a conflict; (5) at the caps the process stays within 8 MiB extra RSS and 64 MiB on disk; at the CI cap the oldest unconfirmed or derived-only CIs are evicted, a new CI is refused and counted (`wrendns_cmdb_dropped_total{kind="ci"}`) when all the rest are authored, and a registry row alone is never treated as authored; and a write-volume test on a stable network shows no row writes except changed records and the batched `last_seen` flush, at most 1 MiB written per day per 1,000 present records; (6) no CMDB value is read by policy, matching, `identify` or naming code (a grep-style test and `dsc_901_*`); (7) `make bench-smoke` shows no change; (8) every setting and action has its control, help topic and Playwright test. *Done 2026-11-19 (track cmdb-core): ADR-1021 to ADR-1024 (Proposed). Step 1 spike: ADR-917's writer is secret-shaped, so the fallback applies (own `cmdb.fetch` RPC). No Pi-hole importer source. AC 5 measured at the caps (65,536 records, 16,384 CIs), two runs: +7.1 MiB RSS (limit 8), 38.8 MiB on disk (limit 64), no rows rewritten in unchanged cycles. `make bench-smoke`: no hot-path crate changed. UI: `/cmdb` page, settings panel, link, unlink, merge and split with previews, four help topics, Playwright `10-cmdb.spec.ts` (5 tests). Deferred to T31.3 to T31.6: definitive sources, MACD, MCP tools, README block. `cargo deny` is not installed in wrendns-dev: not run, and no new crate was added. *Review fixes (track cmdb-core, 2026-11-19):* the Home Assistant feed is written by the discovery poll only (the lease view skipped it: it wrote a second, disagreeing batch under one source name); level 1 hashes every name (proposal text, record keys built from a name, `ap`, `port`, `lldp`, `attached_owner`, `owner`) and a search matches ids, MACs, keys and addresses only; tombstones are kept by count (200,000) with a floor, and a standby behind the floor resyncs in full; a newly designated node always starts a new epoch and a standby only takes the designated node's answer; R5 looks at the whole host-name and network group and compares serials from the records, and the property test now generates host names and networks; a record's attributes are cut to 2 KiB, stored compressed, and a large batch is ingested 128 records at a time; the figures are re-measured with representative records (about 12 attributes, 500 bytes of JSON): +7.1 MiB RSS after a bulk load, +4.0 MiB after a restart, 57.7 MiB on disk, 0 rows rewritten in three unchanged cycles (ADR-1023); the CMDB and the inventory follow the cluster's primary within 10 s of a failover (no node named); the API's CMDB reads run on the blocking pool; the settings panel says nothing reads the numeric settings yet, and the Playwright file round-trips them and shows the privacy level 2 refusal; the CMDB page no longer reloads its list in a loop. **Open:** (a) a node that does not run the CMDB answers 503 for reads and writes (T31.5 step 4 forwards them to the designated node); (b) the passphrase-only backup of authored CMDB data (DSC-906, ADR-1005 section 7) is not built: it is assigned to T31.6 step 6; (c) retention is the ADR-924 constants (7 and 30 days) because `[discovery]` has no `retention_days` setting (ADR-1024); (d) a device keeps a `serial` or `devkey` key row it once held after a split (the records, links and proposals do not depend on it; T31.3 should prune keys no record supports).*
- [ ] **T31.3 Definitive sources and conflicts.** *(DSC-904; ADR-1004)* After T31.2.
  1. The attribute catalog (code) and the resolver with the five-step order, freshness per source kind and the merged value with its deciding source.
  2. `[[cmdb.precedence]]` (admin-only, cap 256) with the Settings table in the UI, ordered per type and attribute, scoped rules, `silent` and `hold_days`.
  3. Per-CI attribute pins, the override list, and manual values (a source), in the CI page and the API.
  4. Silence handling: fallback badge with the definitive value's last value and age; `hold`; the `source_silent` finding.
  5. The conflict view and its actions: Accept, Keep (mute with expiry), raise a MACD.
  6. Mirror a T25.18 `[[group_link]]` read-only (link, group, router, mode with `two_way` shown as `merge`, last round, state) on the CI page and in the conflict view, from shared configuration and the router adapter, never from the sync's `state.db`. `member_of` is a set with the sources `config` and `unifi:<router>`. The mirror is never authoritative, has no control, and CMDB precedence never drives the sync (owner question 13; ADR-998 §14 amended). The sync runs on the primary and the CMDB on the designated node, which can differ.
  7. Caps: 1,024 conflict mutes (oldest first) and 64 pins plus override entries per CI, refused with 409 past the cap. `protected` and a protected attribute's manual value are admin-only.
  - *AC:* (1) each of the five steps overrides the next, with a test per step; (2) a definitive source that goes silent falls back with the badge, and `hold` keeps the value for `hold_days`; (3) a set attribute never conflicts and a single one conflicts only against a fresh source; (4) Accept pins and the conflict disappears, Keep mutes until its expiry; (5) the default order for `device.name` and `interface.addresses` equals ADR-910's, shown by a test over the M25 fixtures; (6) the settings panel round-trips every rule field; help topic and Playwright test; (7) Playwright tests (`cmdb-conflicts.spec.ts`, `cmdb-ci-attributes.spec.ts`) cover the conflict view (Accept, Keep with an expiry, raise a MACD) and the CI page's pin, override-list and manual-value controls, and each control has a help topic; (8) an operator is refused (403, and the control is hidden) when setting `protected` or editing a protected attribute's manual value, an admin succeeds (API test and Playwright); (9) mutes and pins past their caps are refused with 409 and the oldest mute goes first; (10) a linked group shows its T25.18 link read-only and no precedence rule or UI control can change the link's direction (`dsc_904_link_mirror_is_read_only`, `dsc_901_cmdb_never_drives_sync`), and `member_of` from `config` and `unifi:<router>` is a union that never conflicts; (11) when the definitive source goes silent and no fresh next source exists the last value is held and marked stale.
- [ ] **T31.4 MACD lifecycle.** *(DSC-905; ADR-1004, ADR-1005)* After T31.2 (it does not need T31.3 except for conflict-raised records).
  1. The MACD store, the state machine and its transitions, closure reasons, and per-transition history rows with `cmdb.macd.*` audit entries.
  2. The detector: `add`, `move`, `change` and `delete` per ADR-1004 §8, **per source record** (never the merged value), with the per-CI, per-attribute, per-source acknowledged value (advanced on approve and on reject), the **Clear flag** action, the 24 h learning period, the settle time, two-batch debounce, one open record per CI and attribute, and the 200-record cap with a counted overflow. `delete` reads the registry's `days_seen` and CI-level `last_seen`.
  3. Approval rights (viewer, operator, admin, `protected`, agents never, `require_second_approver`) and the verify-and-close of planned changes, with expiry.
  4. The unconfirmed-change alert through the event sinks (`source = "cmdb"`, ADR-102) and `wrendns_cmdb_macd_open{state}`.
  5. The Changes page (inbox, filters, approve, reject, close, bulk approve of detected `add` with a count and preview), the CI page's MACD tab, help topic, Playwright test.
  - *AC:* (1) every legal transition works and every illegal one is refused, as a table test; (2) a detected change approved goes straight to done, a planned one waits for the source to show the end state, and expires after `plan_expiry_days`; (3) AP roaming and address changes raise nothing, a wired port move does; (4) a flapping value inside the settle time raises nothing and a reverted one closes as Withdrawn; (5) nothing is raised in the learning period or after an empty start; (6) an agent token cannot approve, and a request from one carries the owner and reason; (7) the alert fires once after `unconfirmed_alert_hours` and not at privacy level 1 or above; (8) a restart keeps every MACD; (9) a table test of the acknowledged value: approve advances it, reject advances it and sets the flag, the same condition raises no new record on the next settle periods, a further change by the same source raises one, and Clear flag removes the flag (audited); (10) a change of deciding source (the definitive source goes silent, falls to a source that names the port differently, then returns) raises no MACD and writes no history row; (11) `delete` fires for a CI with `days_seen` of at least 3 whose records expired after 7 days and whose CI-level `last_seen` is over 14 days old; (12) an agent token is capped at 50 open requests and 10 creations an hour (429 past that); (13) Clear flag, the Changes page and the CI page's MACD tab have help topics and Playwright tests.

  2. The write API and plan-only agent behaviour (dry run, `Idempotency-Key`, reason, plan id applied by a human).
  3. MCP read tools `search_cmdb_cis`, `get_cmdb_ci`, `list_cmdb_conflicts`, `list_cmdb_macd`, `get_cmdb_macd`, `get_cmdb_status`; plan tools `plan_cmdb_link`, `plan_cmdb_unlink`, `plan_cmdb_value`; the immediate op `request_cmdb_macd` (capped per token); `apply_plan` refuses a CMDB plan from an agent token (human-only apply); `spec/13` catalog updated; snapshot regenerated; device strings marked untrusted.

UI cleanup from the 2026-11-19 audit of the map and its drawer lands on this service. Playwright for each surface, help topics.

## M30 — Query-log negation and a cluster-wide support package (GitHub issues #58 and #55; upstream M24)

  1. **Registry.** `wrendns-config/src/guarded.rs`: one row per guarded setting (`id`, config paths, `mode` of `window`, `immediate`, `staged` or `action`, `weakens(old, new)`, a proof hook for `window` rows, dry-run checks), the table of ADR-956 §1. The rows for T27.14 to T27.17 are added by those tasks. `[auth.oidc] disable_local_login` and `allowed_admin_networks` are deliberately absent (file-only, "No UI" reasons, ADR-956 §1; `api_902_lockout_settings_are_file_only`). `node.data_dir` is present as a `staged` row (T27.17; `api_902_data_dir_is_guarded_and_staged`). `restart-now` is an `action` row with no config path (step 12).
  2. **Storage.** The reserved `node_managed` kind `guarded` (`node/<node-id>/guarded/<id>`), written only by the guarded module and only when a change is final; the generic kind routes refuse it (409 `guarded_only`); files win (409 `set_by_file`); the entry is ignored by an N−1 node.
  3. **Routes** (`/api/v1/guarded`): `GET` (set by file, pending, `pendingRestart`; `config:read`; never `previewId`, `confirmToken` or pending values), `POST /{id}/preview`, `POST /{id}`, `POST /pending/{id}/confirm`, `POST /pending/{id}/cancel`. Role and token checks as ADR-956 §3: admin session only; agent tokens 403 `agent_not_allowed`; other tokens 403 `reauth_required` with a hint; weakening needs a sign-in within 10 minutes; 5 failed confirmations in 10 minutes block the session (429).
  4. **Preview and apply.** The preview returns `previewId`, `phrase`, the effect, `weakening`, `restartRequired`, `wouldDisconnect` and warnings, and is bound to admin, node, setting, value hash and config version (5 minutes; 409 `preview_stale`). Apply checks `previewId` and `confirm` on the server and answers 200 `applied`, 202 `staged` or 202 `pending`.
  5. **Window state machine** on the target node: one pending change per node (409 `guarded_change_pending`); `[api] confirm_window_secs` (default 120, 30 to 600, file-only, added to the schema); the `deadlineSecs` measured on the monotonic clock; the single-use `confirmToken`; confirmation proved by a per-row hook that returns `new_socket`, `new_cert` or `proxy_list` (a TLS-only change gets a temporary parallel listener on a port named in the preview); a pending proxy list applies only to the confirm route until confirmed; rollback on expiry, cancel, failed commit or failed bind, with reasons; a restart inside the window starts with the previous values.
  6. **Staging and probation.** `staged` entries are written at once and listed as `pendingRestart` (the `data-dir` pointer is read first from the file-named directory's `state.db`, and the sidecar stays there); start-up marks staged and restored entries on probation, with the failed-start counter in the sidecar `<data_dir>/guarded-probation` (fsync before the guarded values apply); healthy means the state opened, the API listener bound, the node's own DNS probe answered and (for `secrets-key`) the store is unlocked, within `max(confirm_window_secs, 180)`; two failed starts drop them, but never back to the old key alone once any row was re-encrypted; a bind failure for a confirmed guarded listener falls back for that start (`guarded_bind_fallback`).
  7. **Cluster.** Only the primary forwards a request for another node over the cluster channel, with an assertion (admin, role, sign-in time, expiry) signed by the primary that the target verifies (a replica's is refused); the pending change and confirmation stay on the target; the entry is written through the primary (409 `primary_unreachable` when it can't be reached); no "all nodes" apply.
  8. **Audit and alerts.** `settings.guarded`, `settings.guarded_rolled_back` (reasons `expired`, `cancelled`, `commit_failed`, `bind_failed`, `failed_start`) and `settings.guarded_refused`; the alert condition `guarded_setting_changed` on apply and on outcome; credentials redacted in before and after.
  9. **Agents.** No tool, plan or scope; the plan store refuses guarded paths; the spec/13 §3 list gains the routes and the new problem codes.
  10. **Recovery** (ADR-957): `wrendns guarded list` and `clear` (offline, audited with `cli:<os user>`), `WRENDNS_IGNORE_GUARDED=1` with the health reason `guarded_ignored`, the local suppression of a cleared entry until the primary's copy changes (and the removal request on reconnect), and `docs/recovery.md` (the symptom and fix table).
  11. **UI.** `GuardedChange.svelte` (preview, red "weakens security" mark, the phrase, the sign-in prompt, the countdown from `deadlineSecs`, Confirm and Cancel, the confirm step opened from the URL fragment on the new address, "pending restart" with the restart steps, the rollback message and reason, and the "Restart now" flow of step 12) and a `guarded.svelte.ts` store; "set by file" locks the control. No setting is wired to it until T27.14; the Playwright tests here use a test-only registry row (an `immediate` and a `window` one) compiled only under the cargo feature `e2e` (never behind an environment variable alone; the e2e server is built with it, the release binary is not). The exit hook of step 12 is gated the same way: it exists only under `e2e`, so no environment variable in a release build can turn a restart into a no-op.

- [ ] **T27.14 Listeners, API address and TLS, trusted proxies.** *(API-902, CLU-006, CLU-004, DNS-001; ADR-914, ADR-956)* After T27.13. The four `window` settings on Settings → System, per node, each a registry row.
  1. **Listeners.** A form for `[[listen]]` (address, port, protocol, TLS). `Listeners` gains stage, commit and abort: the new sockets are bound next to the old ones for the whole window, the old ones close only on commit, a failed bind changes nothing and reports the address and the error. The confirmation proof (`new_socket`) is that the node's own probe of the new listener answers (an encrypted listener is probed over its protocol).
  2. **API address and TLS.** Forms for `api.listen` and `api.tls`.   3. **Trusted proxies.** A form for `api.trusted_proxies`; the proof (`proxy_list`) is that the confirming request passes under the new list, and the confirm step shows the client address the server now sees; until confirmed the new list is used by the confirm route only.

Owner decision, 2026-11-26 (against the design note's recommendation; design note §2.7): on a node whose web UI the admin's browser cannot open, the primary may pass the admin's confirm of a `listen` change on to that node with the admin's signed identity. The mechanism below (lifetimes, checks, caps) is the design note's proposal, not an owner decision; the owner has not yet accepted its residual risks. The primary: `POST /api/v1/guarded/pending/{id}/confirm-relay` for an interactive admin session (agents 403 `agent_not_allowed`, other tokens 403 `reauth_required`, operators and viewers 403; a replica answers 421 `not_primary`) with the change's `confirmToken` in the body; it keeps, for the window, the forwarded changes it carried (pending ID, preview ID, node, setting, admin, value digest); refuses any setting but `listen`, a target that is the primary itself or standalone, a session of another admin, and for a weakening change a sign-in older than 10 minutes; audits `settings.guarded_confirm_relayed` before sending (no audit, no relay) and the outcome after; signs a relayed-confirm assertion whose `purpose` is `confirm` (setting, node, pending ID, preview ID, value digest, admin, role, session digest, sign-in time, the browser's reported address, `issuedAt`, `expiresAt` at most 30 seconds later and never past the window, a 128-bit nonce) and sends it with the token over the mTLS cluster channel; the token is never logged or audited. The target checks, itself: the sender is the primary's node ID and key; the setting and the pending change are both `listen`; the pending ID, node, preview ID, value digest and admin match the pending change; the token matches (constant time) and is unused; `expiresAt - issuedAt` is at most 30 seconds, not past on its clock with a 5-second allowance, and the pending change is still open on its monotonic window; the nonce is unused (kept in memory for the life of the change and at least 60 seconds); recency for a weakening change; at most 5 refused relays per change (a refusal only because a probe has not answered yet is not counted); then every DNS probe answers and the host facts match, as for a direct confirm. Any failure is 403 `relay_refused` with the reason and `settings.guarded_refused`; success writes `settings.guarded` with `confirmedVia: "primary"`, the primary's node ID and the nonce, and the alert says "confirmed through the primary". The window is not lengthened and rollback is unchanged. UI: the preview's note when the reachability check fails, and "Confirm through the primary" on the countdown for a `listen` change on another node. Help: the `listeners` paragraph "Confirming through the primary", which also says what a relayed confirm does not prove (design note §2.7's residual risks); `docs/recovery.md`; spec/13 §3 gains the route and the code; the `spec/01` row API-904 is added when this task starts.

## M26 — Live network map (owner request 2026-11-16) [fork #14]

An animated, live map of the network and of where its lookups go, coloured by health: green healthy, yellow warnings, red errors. It has two views: the **network map** (gateway → networks/VLANs → devices, the WrenDNS nodes and their upstreams, with query flows animated along the links) and the **world view** (arcs to where answers point, using an optional IP-to-country database downloaded at runtime, never in the image). Flows are DNS lookups, not packets. It is built only on existing streams and counters, so nothing is added to the query path. Every control is in the UI. Topology gets richer once M25's SNMP/LLDP data exists, but the first version runs on M22's inventory.

- [x] **T26.1 Design ADR.** *(OBS-901, OBS-902)* No UI: a design record. A Proposed ADR: the data sources (query tail, time buckets, upstream and cluster health, inventory), server-side sampling with a cap per second, the health classification (green/yellow/red from the SLO and health settings), the map API (snapshot + stream) and MCP read tool, the GeoIP source, licence, download, verification and updates, the rendering approach (SVG/Canvas, no heavy library, within the 400 KiB UI budget), and cluster behaviour. *Done 2026-11-17: ADR-958 (the map: data model, the sampler on the aggregator thread, classification and `[map]` settings, API, cluster, privacy, SVG rendering, animation and accessibility, test plan) and ADR-959 (GeoIP: DB-IP Country Lite, CC BY 4.0, admin opt-in download, verification, on-disk lookup), both Proposed. Found: `QueryEvent` has no answer address, so T26.2 step 1 adds one behind a benchmark gate, with a fallback to upstream markers. T26.2 to T26.6 below are refined into steps.*
- [ ] **T26.2 Map data API and health classification.** *(OBS-901, AGT-001..005, CLU-002; ADR-958)* Snapshot and stream routes, OpenAPI, an MCP `network_health` read tool, the federated cluster read. UI: the map pages (T26.3, T26.5); T26.2 isn't ticked before their Playwright tests pass against it.

## M25 — Network inventory: SNMP, gateway reads and imported scans (owner request 2026-11-16) [fork #15]

This milestone gathers what the network already knows, and what the owner's own scans found. It follows on from M22 ("Network inventory and home integrations"):
- a read-only SNMP poller of listed gateways and switches, plus identity reads of hosts that routers or L2 tables already see;
- more read-only UniFi and Home Assistant reads;
- uploads of the owner's nmap or CSV results;
- one inventory keyed by MAC across every source.

WrenDNS itself never probes (ADR-907): no sweeps, no ICMP, TCP, ARP or mDNS solicitation, no scheduled scans. Everything is off by default and runs on one designated node. SNMP runs in a separate worker process, and import parsing in another, so neither can take DNS down (CLU-004). The inventory never feeds policy or DNS names (ADR-910).

Each task:
- ships its own UI controls, help topics and Playwright tests (the standing rule at the top of this file); T25.14 is the walk-through and help review;
- updates `docs/` and `site/guide-devices.html` for whatever it makes visible (DOC-006);
- regenerates OpenAPI, `ui/src/api-types.ts` and `docs/config-schema.json` when its schema changes;
- records its image delta with `deploy/image/size.py --oci` on amd64, arm64 and arm/v7.

The deltas are summed per architecture against a milestone stop line of 0.08 MiB. T25.0 records the measured per-architecture image size from the image job, so the headroom after M23 is a measured number, not an estimate.

Order:
1. T25.0 first.
2. T25.1, T25.2 and T25.3 can start at once.
3. `SecretValue` and `Credential::resolve` land in T23.3, so T25.4 needs T23.1–T23.3, or defines `SecretValue` itself.
4. `*_ref` and the UI fields need T23.3–T23.6. Replicated refs need T23.5.

  - *Done in part (fix: review fixes for m25-snmp, 2026-11-17):* authNoPriv and authPriv over the connected agent. Engine discovery accepts only a noAuthNoPriv Report whose varbind is `usmStatsUnknownEngineIDs`, and a failed exchange drops the cached engine. The time window follows RFC 3414 §3.2.7b (higher boots or a later time resyncs; lower boots, or equal boots more than 150 s behind, is stale; boots at 2^31-1 is stale). An authenticated notInTimeWindow Report takes the agent's clock and the request is sent once more, at most once per agent per minute. The reply must match the request's security level, engine ID and user. Ku and the privacy key are zeroized; the MAC and the community are compared in constant time. - [ ] **T25.18 UniFi device and group sync.** [owner request 2026-11-18] *(DSC-016, DSC-017, API-016, AGT-001..005; ADR-998, ADR-999 (both Proposed), amends ADR-912's "reads only")* Depends on T25.10, the router integration (M22, M23) and **T24.30** (the preview's before-and-after effective policy uses its resolver; if T24.30 is not done when step 5 is built, the preview ships without the policy column and that is recorded Open here). **Design is this entry and the two ADRs; nothing is built until the owner accepts ADR-998 and ADR-999.** The sync keeps the membership of a WrenDNS group and one UniFi group object the same, in either direction chosen per link. It syncs **membership only**; categories and policy are not mapped (ADR-998 §11). The premise that UniFi's content filtering is traffic-level, not DNS-level, is unconfirmed and public sources say the opposite (ADR-998) and suggest UniFi Content Filter on a synced group may redirect DNS to the gateway and so bypass WrenDNS for it; the product text claims neither stacking nor IP-level enforcement until the owner confirms (Q4).
  - **Decide the order of work.** Steps 1 and 2 are small and safe and come first; the read-only direction (steps 3 to 7) is useful without ADR-999; the write steps (8, 9) need both ADRs accepted.
  - **1. Capability check (no code on the DNS path, no request to a real gateway by anyone but its owner).** Find out which UniFi object holds device-group members and how to read and write it, from the gateway's own OpenAPI document (`/proxy/network/api-docs/integration.json`), which **the owner downloads** (it may be committed as a fixture only after it is checked for site IDs and any other identifier), or from the owner's browser's network log of creating a device group (**a HAR or network log carries the session cookie, `x-csrf-token` and real MACs: it stays outside the repository and is never committed or pushed; only a hand-written, redacted summary goes into `docs/unifi-sync-capabilities.md`**; a secret-scan or redaction check (grep for cookie, token, key and MAC patterns) runs on every file the step commits); record the path, the member form (MAC or client ID), whether offline clients are members, the write method, the CSRF need, the role a key or user needs, and whether UniFi's admin log shows the write. Output: a short `docs/unifi-sync-capabilities.md` and an update to ADR-998 §2 (the first backend kind), or a note that no API exists, which stops the task at this step and is reported to the owner. Decision Q1 covers how it is done.
  - **2. The pure merge.** `crates/wrendns/src/unifi_sync/merge.rs` (no I/O): inputs B, U, T (sets of MACs with flags `private`, `syncable`), the mode, the guard limits; output a `Plan` of changes by side and device, the held and conflict items, and the reasons for each skip. Property tests: convergence, idempotence (applying the plan then merging again gives an empty plan), no removal without a baseline, no oscillation, a change on both sides in the same way is a no-op, and unsyncable devices are never touched.
  - **3. The read client.** `GroupBackend::list_objects` and `::members` for the first kind over the router's existing session or key (the inventory thread's shared session, ADR-912; the read credential only). Row and byte caps as T25.10 (4 MiB, 8,192 rows). Device strings are untrusted (DSC-015).
  - **4. Links and settings.** `[[group_link]]` as a shared managed kind `group_links` (`/api/v1/group-links[/{id}]`; create, change of mode and unlink are admin-only; an operator may pause) and `[unifi_sync]` (`enabled`, `writes_enabled`, `interval_secs`, `max_changes_per_round`, `mass_change_percent`, `baseline_max_age`, `stale_alert_rounds`) as an admin-only singleton `unifi-sync` (an operator or agent may only turn `enabled` off). Validation: the group and router exist, one link per group per router, one link per UniFi object, `kind` known. Regenerate OpenAPI, config schema, UI types and the MCP snapshot.
  - **5. The preview and the apply (read direction).** `POST /api/v1/group-links/{id}/preview` (read, off the query path, bounded; returns the plan with a `preview_id`, each device's before and after effective policy from the T24.30 resolver, the skipped and private and unmatched lists, the held items) and `POST /api/v1/group-links/{id}/apply` with the `preview_id` (409 `preview_stale` if either side changed). The WrenDNS-side changes are config writes through the normal path with `origin = sync:<id>`, one audit record per change, and created devices `[[client]] name, match = [mac], groups = [group]`.
  - **6. The sync thread, on the primary.** Its own thread and runtime like the inventory (ADR-912, ADR-930's gate: not an ephemeral pod, not a witness, only the primary), a timer at `interval_secs`, one round per link at a time, baselines in `state.db` (sent best-effort to peers, a missing one makes the link held and additive-only), stale and flapping states, `wrendns_unifi_sync_*` metrics (rounds, changes by side and kind, held, conflicts, stale links, write failures), alerts `unifi_sync_stale` and `unifi_sync_flapping`.
  - **7. The conflict view.** `GET /api/v1/group-links/{id}/conflicts` and `POST .../resolve` (per row: take UniFi, take WrenDNS, keep both, skip), shaped like T31.3's conflict rows so M31 can absorb it.
  - **8. The write client (ADR-999; after the owner accepts it).** `unifi_write::member_op` as the only function that holds the write credential and builds a write; `write_api_key_ref` and `write_username`/`write_password_ref` on `[[router]]` through the M23 store (`SecretField`, `discovery`-style names `router.<name>.write_api_key`); audit before the request; one write a second, 50 changes a round; no redirects; the pinned TLS settings; verify by re-read before the baseline advances; the Check button (one GET of the target object with the write credential, the single stated exception, and the account's role only if that same GET's response carries it; no second call); the **verify re-read uses the read credential**; a session-only local user as the fallback if keys need a super admin (password through M23, CSRF handled); write credential replication limited to nodes that can become primary.
  - **9. Write modes.** `wrendns_definitive` and `two_way` in the merge's apply, behind `writes_enabled` and the admin's applied preview; **entering a write mode, or `writes_enabled` off to on, holds every affected link until a fresh preview is applied; applied state lives in `state.db`, and links from file, Git or a restore start preview-only and held;** a synced add appends the group last in a client's `groups` and a removal removes only that entry; an agent-originated membership change on a write-mode linked group is refused with 403 `agent_not_allowed`; a parseable empty read when B was not is held as a preview; *Undo last round*; the flapping pause; the mass-change guard in both directions.
  - **10. API, MCP and agents.** Every operation in OpenAPI with dry run, `Idempotency-Key` and reason (AGT-001..006); MCP read tools `list_group_links`, `get_group_link_preview`, `get_unifi_sync_status` and plan tools `plan_link_group`, `plan_set_group_link_mode`, `plan_unlink_group`; no agent scope applies a preview or a plan that writes to UniFi (403 `agent_not_allowed`, as ADR-903 §5), and `apply_plan` refuses an `agent:*` change that alters the membership of a write-mode linked group; spec/13 rows; a plan response says `propagates_to_unifi` for a group in a write mode.
  - **11. UI (standing rule).**
    - Groups page, per group, a **Linked to UniFi** card: the link state chip (in sync, held, stale, flapping, broken, paused); **Link to UniFi…** (admin) opens a dialog: router, the UniFi objects read from the gateway (searchable, a same-name one only suggested), mode as three radio choices with one sentence each (UniFi is definitive, WrenDNS is definitive, both ways), and the switches *Create missing devices* and *Include private MACs*; **Preview** (a table by side and device with the badges *private MAC*, *no MAC, skipped*, *unmatched*, each device's change in effective policy, and a held banner with the reason), **Apply** (admin, only the previewed plan), Pause, **Unlink** (says it deletes nothing). A banner on a linked group's membership editor, for any role, says a change reaches UniFi in the write modes. The link dialog and the card show the warning **"UniFi Content Filter on this group may bypass WrenDNS"**; changing the mode to a write mode, or turning writes on, shows the link as *held* with the text that a new preview is needed.
    - Settings or the Network inventory page: the **UniFi sync** card (admin): the `enabled` and `writes_enabled` switches (the second disabled with the reason until a write credential is set), the intervals, the write credential through `SecretField` on the Routers page's UniFi entry, the Check button with its result.

Docs and site.** `docs/unifi-sync.md` (what syncs and what does not, the private-MAC note, the first-sync walk-through, the security note on who can change a linked group, outages, the kill switches, how to remove it, and the warning that UniFi Content Filter on a synced group may bypass WrenDNS), `docs/security.md` (the first write to the gateway), the Routers page text, `docs/configuration.md`, `site/guide-devices.html`.

Open from the start (recorded, not built).** Showing read-only which UniFi policies and content-filter profiles use a linked group; creating the UniFi group from a WrenDNS group; syncing a display name (the only place last-writer-wins would apply); other object kinds (`usergroup`, `firewallgroup`); writing any UniFi policy; whether UniFi's own admin log records the write.

Does the owner accept that exposure for the write modes? [accept only with the read direction first; otherwise refuse ADR-999]

## Worker fixes (track worker-rlimit)
- [x] **T-wl Sandboxed workers in the musl release build and the image.** *(API-007, DSC-002; ADR-988, ADR-989)* The Pi-hole import worker answered `"<path>: <path>"` in every musl build and the image had no `/tmp` for it. mimalloc's 1 GiB arena counted against `RLIMIT_DATA`; workers now start with `MIMALLOC_ARENA_RESERVE=0` (set by `prepare_spawn`), `harden` refuses a limit the process already exceeds and says why, and the import's scratch files live in `<data_dir>/import-tmp/<unique>` (0700, removed afterwards).
  - *Done (track worker-rlimit, 2026-11-18):* `wrendns-net` `worker.rs` and `sys.rs` (`WORKER_ALLOCATOR_ENV`, the `harden` preflight, `vm_data_bytes`); `pihole_import.rs` (`Upload` scratch directory, `--scratch`), `pihole.rs` (`load_in`); tests `crates/wrendns/tests/pihole_import_worker.rs` (3, spawn the built binary under the real limit), `dsc_002_prepare_spawn_sets_allocator_env`, `dsc_002_vm_data_is_readable`, `api_007_upload_scratch_*` (2), and `discovery_workers.rs` started through `prepare_spawn`; `deploy/worker-image-e2e.sh` and the CI job `worker-image` (musl image, read-only root, no `/tmp`: discovery handshake and a gravity.db and a Teleporter zip through the API). No setting, route or tool was added, so no UI control, help topic or Playwright test applies. Reproduced first with a `bench-fast` musl build (`docker buildx build --target bin`) and `strace`. Also found: the discovery worker's limit had bounded nothing (its allocations stayed inside the pre-mapped arena); it is now a real bound.
  - *Review fixes:* the temp-dir fallback no longer chmods or sweeps the system temp directory (ADR-989 amended), entry cap 256 MiB, ADR-988 reworded. Open: a release-build test that the discovery worker's limit aborts an allocation (the `alloc` fault op is debug-only by design, `dsc_002_release_has_no_fault_ops`); the 256 MiB archive cap means no archive can now provoke the abort, so the image check covers only the handshake and the refusal when the variable is missing.
  - *Open:* the CLI `wrendns import pihole` of an archive still uses the system's temporary directory (it runs in an operator's shell); the arm64 and armv7 images were not run here (CI builds amd64; the same zigbuild path and allocator apply).

## Test fixes (fork #20)
- [x] **T-f20 `ups_005` parallel race test.** [fork #20] *(UPS-005; ADR-974)* `ups_005_parallel_races_and_first_answer_wins` no longer checks a 150 ms bound, which measured the UDP bind cost of wrendns-dev (about 10 ms each, queued across the process; `bench/README.md`) and not the race. It checks that the first good answer is the fast member's, that the group returns before the slow member's attempt cap (1 s), and that it hands the fast answer back within 150 ms of the fast member sending it (a gap with no bind in it). The slow member's own timeout is above that cap, so only a group that waits for it would take longer. `ups_006_single_member_waits_for_a_slow_answer` now bounds its budget check at 500 ms, below the 600 ms slow answer. The product is unchanged. A fan-out delay below 1 s is not separated from bind cost by a timing check here (ADR-974, open). *AC:* 20 consecutive parallel runs of `cargo test -p wrendns-upstream --test upstream` pass in wrendns-dev (done: 20 of 20, 14 of 14 each, 67 to 106 s); after the review fixes, three further full runs of the binary pass 14 of 14 (66 to 69 s); clippy and fmt clean; a group that waits for every member fails at 1.00 s (checked by mutation). *Done 2026-11-17: `crates/wrendns-upstream/tests/upstream.rs`. Open (ADR-974, Proposed): the per-query UDP bind in Docker Desktop, which caps cache misses near 100 a second there; removing it from the query path is the owner's decision and needs a benchmark on quiet hardware (T24.22).*

## M24 — Replacing Pi-hole (owner request 2026-11-16)

What a home running a Pi-hole pair behind a keepalived VIP needs to switch to WrenDNS and keep running it: Pi-hole's special names, "Update Gravity", the importer's gaps, and the failover pieces. The UniFi integration (M22) is the edge Pi-hole never had. Benchmarks from Docker Desktop don't count for the 5% rule (every UDP `bind()` there takes about 10 ms; `bench/README.md`), so each hot-path task reruns `make bench-smoke` on the homelab before release. Open items are also filed as GitHub issues on the fork (`nbacheller/wrendns`), written "fork #N" here to tell them from upstream's issue numbers. Items of the hosted service are tracked in WrenDNS Cloud's own private tracker and written "cloud #N". Fork-wide items without a task: #10 (tests that fail on a CRLF checkout), #11 (Windows `nslookup` on port 1053), #12 (Home Assistant source untested against a real instance). Upstream issues to take when fixed, checked at each sync: upstream #7 (the process stops answering on every port while the service stays up) and upstream #43 (a replica attached to another replica never moves back to the primary).

- [x] **T24.11 Shared missing-set race.** [fork #8] *(CLU-003, OBS-009)* `Federated::missing` is one shared mutex, so two `GET /lists` requests at the same time can overwrite each other's `missingNodes`. Give each request its own missing set (or compute it per call) so a replica's answer names only the nodes its own reads missed. Also: `GET /lists` on a replica makes two serial reads (`Read::Lists` then `Read::ListHits`), up to 2 s each, so one request can take about 4 s; run both in one round. No UI: an internal fix.
  - *Done 2026-11-17 (track missingrace):* a request's missing set is its own. `Backend::for_request` gives each request a handle with its own `missing` cell (`crate::request_backend` in `wrendns-api`, called by every handler that returns `missingNodes`), so one request's missing nodes never show in another's answer (`Federated::for_request`). The federated gather is now a round that returns its missing set (`Federated::round`); nothing is written to a shared cell. `GET /lists` asks the primary's lists and every node's hits in one round (`Backend::lists_and_hits`, `ListsAndHits { lists, hits, missing }`), so it takes one deadline instead of two, and its handler no longer resets the set between two reads. API shapes are unchanged; no DNS hot-path change, no UI (an internal fix). Test: `clu_003_concurrent_requests_name_only_their_own_missing_nodes` (a replica of a silent primary: the first request names the primary, a concurrent second request on the same backend names nothing); it fails when per-request handles are disabled. Tests: `cargo test -p wrendns` 592 passed, 1 ignored (the 5 integration binaries pass); `cargo test -p wrendns-api` 165 passed. No ADR: the task text already names the per-request set. Captured with a logging relay on 127.0.0.1:53 forwarding to the bundle's 1053 (no packet reached a relay on the chosen port in any run). - [ ] **T24.25 Pre-bound UDP sockets for upstream queries.** [fork #20] *(UPS-005, NFR-*; ADR-974)* **Owner decision 2026-11-18: build behind a benchmark.** In Docker Desktop each upstream UDP query waits 10 to 20 ms for its socket bind (ADR-974), which caps cache misses near 100 a second. Build a bounded stock of pre-bound sockets, each used for one query and then closed, refilled off the query path, so the source port stays random per query (RFC 5452) and nothing on the cache-hit path changes. Write the ADR first (stock size, refill, what happens when it is empty: bind inline as today).
  - *AC:* measured on quiet hardware with T24.22: cache-miss throughput and p99 with and without the stock, on Linux and in Docker Desktop; merged only if it is better on both and no worse on the cache-hit path; RSS within budget; source ports pass a randomness check over 10,000 queries.
- [ ] **T24.26 Lease lapses with a witness.** [fork] *(CLU-005; ADR-947, ADR-960, ADR-990)* On a three-node Raspberry Pi test cluster (node-b primary, node-a eligible replica, node-c witness; auto failover, voters 3) the primary logged "this primary's lease lapsed; publishing paused until a majority renews it" every 10 to 20 minutes and once 14 s after adopting `auto`. A lapse needs the renewal rounds at 5 s and 10 s both unanswered (the lease is 13 s from the send of the last granted round), so something systematic held answers for seconds. Cause found by reading the path: every renewal moved `Ballot::lease_until_ms`, so each voter, and the primary for its own grant, wrote and fsynced `ballot.json` on every 5 s round, under the election lock (and on the voter's request handler); on an SD card a slow fsync (other writers on the card, flash housekeeping) held the answer past the 2 s ask deadline, and on the primary it held the election task and delayed the round's sends while the lease was already counting from the round's start. A renewal now stores nothing (`Ballot::must_persist_since`): only a vote or a first lease reaches the disk, since the stored lease is on a process clock that is never read back (`Ballot::adopt` gives a restarted node a full lease); a new elector starts from the running one's ballot, or from a stored one with a full lease from now (`Ballot::for_new_elector`), so the lease it promised is never shortened. Diagnostics added: debug lines for each renewal round (sent; ended with its grants, the majority needed and the lease left), for each vote answer (voter, granted, `took_ms`) and for a request with no answer (error, `took_ms`); an info line and a `lease_renewed` event when a lapsed lease is renewed again, with how long publishing paused; a warning when storing the ballot takes 500 ms or more. *AC:* `clu_005_t24_26_a_renewal_is_not_stored`, `clu_005_t24_26_the_primarys_own_renewal_is_not_stored` (both fail without the fix: every renewal asked for a store) and `clu_005_t24_26_a_new_elector_never_shortens_a_lease` pass; the cluster crate's 82 library tests and the partition simulator pass; clippy and fmt clean; `deploy/cluster3/e2e.sh` passes (a to i); the soak `deploy/cluster3/lapse-soak.sh` (two eligible nodes and a witness, its own project) runs with no lapse. *Done 2026-11-18: `crates/wrendns-cluster/src/{election,failover,net,node}.rs`, `deploy/cluster3/{lapse-soak.sh,compose-lapse.yaml,config/witness.toml}`, ADR-990 (Proposed). Open: the lapse was not reproduced in Docker, where a per-container write cap (`DISK_DEV`, `WRITE_BPS`) slows the ballot store (three "slow" warnings in 300 s at 8 KB/s) but never held a round past 2 s, so the cause is established by code and the fsync count, not by a failing soak; the Pi cluster is the test (after the upgrade, a lapse now shows its debug lines at `WRENDNS_LOG=debug`). A lapse 14 s after adopting `auto` is not explained by this: if it recurs, the first-round debug lines will show which voter answered late. The vote RPC still shares its stream with large transfers (head-of-line blocking); not changed here (no evidence it is the cause).*
  - **Review fixes 2026-11-18 (reopened):** the cause is a hypothesis, not proven (no reproduction; the base image also had no lapse in the soak, so the soak cannot tell old from fixed). More likely causes sit on the primary: a slow fsync of its own grant, or the vote RPC queued behind large transfers (both voters are fed from the primary). Done in the second review fix: (1) `crates/wrendns-cluster/tests/lapse.rs` drives the real `Elector` with a modelled store delay: at 2, 2.5 and 4 s the base policy lapses and the fix does not, and neither lapses at 0 or 0.3 s (this shows the mechanism, not that the Pis' stores are that slow). Still to do: (2) run a diagnostics-only build on the Pis and compare slow-store warnings with the lapse times; (3) check what the primary runs every 10 to 20 minutes (blocklist refresh, snapshot or discovery transfers) against the lapse times. Fixed in review: a deposed or manual-mode node (`end_lease_lapse_for_manual_mode`) no longer logs "publishing resumes" or emits `lease_renewed`; `WRENDNS_LOG` takes per-module directives (`info,wrendns_cluster::failover=debug`); the slow-store warning is limited to one a minute with a held-back count; `lease_lost` and `lease_renewed` have labels on the Cluster page (Playwright `clu_005 lease lapse and renewal events have labels`); soak variable renamed `PAUSE_S` (it pauses a node, not a disk). Not done: names in vote-answer lines (voter ids map to nodes with `wrendns cluster status`); a lapse-time warning naming missing voters (needs round history; deferred until the cause is reproduced).

  1. **Known `WRENDNS_*` variables.** The shipped unit, bundles and chart set `WRENDNS_SUPERVISOR` (T27.13) and the env reader warned "ignoring unknown environment variable" at every start. The reader now lists every `WRENDNS_*` variable the binary reads outside the config (`SUPERVISOR`, `IGNORE_GUARDED`, `TOKEN`, `LOG_DNSSEC_LIBRARY`, the plugin's `PLUGIN_SOCKET` and `UPSTREAM`, and the test hooks `SIM_SCHEDULES`, `SIM_SEED`, `TEST_WALK`).
  2. **GitHub page and regex adlists in the import.** `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/blob/<ref>/<path>` (and `/raw/`) becomes `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<o>/<r>/<ref>/<path>`, and the preview notes say so. An adlist whose file is named like a regex list (`regex.list`, `regex.txt`) is not imported: Pi-hole adlists hold domains or hosts lines, so the preview says it can't work as a list and to add the patterns as regex deny rules.
  3. **A list over its size limit is fixable from the Lists page.** The failure says the limit (and the size the server announced, now in the error); "Raise the limit to N MiB" sets that list's own `max_bytes` (the announced size plus a quarter, or double the old limit; never above 128 MiB, the most one list may take on the small-device budgets) and downloads it again. Over 128 MiB the row says to remove it or use a smaller list.
  4. **A 404 is said plainly.** A list whose address returns 404 or 410 shows "not found: moved or deleted by its maintainer. Remove it, or replace it with the list's new address", with a Remove button that asks first.
  5. **Prune.** A list whose every name is in another list (Unique 0) says so and offers Turn it off and Remove.

No API or schema change (the UI reads the existing error text and uses the existing list endpoints), so OpenAPI and the config schema are unchanged. Open: the size seen is only known when the server announces it (Content-Length); a chunked download is cut at the limit, so the suggestion is then double the old limit. Merged feat/ipam-integrations again (its T27.11 `[filter]` settings kind and this task's are one kind with four keys, one card on the Lists page: ADR-1017 item 10); tests after the merge: config 78+55+2+1, filter 49+23+7+1, policy 34+1, api 289, wrendns 860+1+15+1+3+1+1, support 53, Playwright 1-ui and 8-settings 215 and 9-categories 7, all passing; `make bench-smoke` could not pass on this host (a UDP bind costs 10 ms on Docker Desktop and other waves load the CPUs: both the branch's binary and an earlier build of it lose 30 to 85 % of the queries), so it is Open for a quiet host; no dependency was added, so `cargo deny` (not installed in `wrendns-dev`) was not run; ADR-1017 items 8 and 9 (Proposed).

Playwright `1-ui` failed after the merge because a page reload right after Apply cancelled the in-flight write (the request future was dropped between planning and applying): a configuration write now runs to its end whatever the client does (`api_010_a_write_survives_the_client_hanging_up`); `1-ui` 210/210. The UI size gate is the owner's 512 KiB (ADR-1020): 437.3 KiB.

- [ ] **T24.39 Browser and endpoint agent: temporary site exceptions, plus DNS and URL history.** [owner request 2026-11-18, extended 2026-11-19, fork #29] *(FLT-006, ADR-067 quick rules, T24.29 categories, T24.30 policy, ADR-102 privacy levels, DSC-901 (the device's CMDB CI); new FLT-9xx and OBS-9xx requirements; ADR)*
  - **Extended 2026-11-19 (owner):** the local endpoint agent also captures the device's **DNS and URL history**, because the resolver sees domains only and misses full URLs, the browsers' own DoH, cached answers and roaming. Scope (details in fork #29): URL history from the same MV3 extension (top-level navigations; query strings and fragments stripped by default, per-group detail: host, host and path, or full URL; private windows off by default); DNS history from the extension's `webRequest` hosts and, optionally, a native device agent for every app (Windows DNS Client ETW first; owner decision); batched upload with the device-scoped token, an offline queue, caps and rate limits; records attached to the device's CMDB CI; stored apart from the query log with its own retention, replicated, off at privacy level 1 and above unless allowed per group, never in an unencrypted backup; consent and visibility (recording indicator, the person can see their own history, **history off for every group by default**: an admin turns it on per group, with the recording notice on the device (owner, 2026-11-19: WrenDNS is not aimed at minors, so no children's-group default and no marketing as parental monitoring), force-install through browser policy, "agent not reporting" on the device page); a **Browsing** tab on the device page that joins URLs with the DNS lookups they caused and any blocks; API and MCP reads behind a new sensitive scope `history:read` in no default grant, audited, redacted to the host for agents unless the scope allows paths. Four more owner decisions (URL detail, retention, native agent, private windows) join the six below; the default (off for every group) is decided.
  - **Why both:** a block page can only appear for plain HTTP. An HTTPS site shows a certificate error first, and HSTS-preloaded sites can't be clicked through. So the browser add-on is the dependable route and the landing page is the fallback.
  - **Owner decisions first** (asked together, with "accept all recommendations"): self-serve or approval per group; the durations and daily caps; categories that are never excepted; which browsers; store listings or self-hosted only; whether to serve a plain-HTTP block page at all; and, for history, the URL detail kept, retention, a native agent or browser-only for v1, and private windows.
  - **Steps:**
    1. **Exception requests:** stored, audited and replicated. Per-group self-serve limits or approval. Approve or deny with one click, which creates a device-scoped quick rule. A notification through the UI badge and the alert sinks.
    2. **Device-scoped tokens:** paired by QR code or a code. A token can only request or self-serve its own device's exceptions, within limits and rate limited, and is never an admin token.
    3. **Landing page `/unblock`:** phone-width, with Explain's reason and the request or self-serve controls.
    4. **MV3 extension** (Chrome/Edge first) in the repo. It detects a block from the navigation error plus an "is `<host>` blocked for me, and why?" API call, and sends only the host name.
    5. **API and MCP:** agents can read requests; approval is plan-only.
    6. **Tests and docs:** help topics, Playwright for the page, extension tests with the extension loaded, the cluster e2e (a request made on a replica appears on the primary), and docs.

- [x] **T24.37 Entries added through the API stay editable after a failover.** [owner report 2026-11-18] *(CLU-015, CLU-004, API-010, API-016, AGT-001; ADR-1016 (Proposed))* **Owner report:** the Pi-hole import was applied through the API while node-b was primary; after an automatic failover node-a was primary, `GET /api/v1/upstreams` listed `pihole-1` and node-a served it, but `DELETE /api/v1/upstreams/pihole-1` (and `?dryRun=true`) answered 404 `no pihole-1`. The entry was in node-a's `published-config.json` and not in its managed store or files.
  - *Cause (established with a failing test first):* a replica applies the shared configuration and keeps no rows; a promoted primary builds on that version and looks entries up in its own rows and files, so the API's entries of every shared kind were served but not its own, and a delete that did work would have come back from the inherited version.
  - *Fix (ADR-1016):* the primary publishes its shared-kind rows whole in the `node_managed` blob; a node promoted from replica replaces its rows with the inherited blob once per blob (so a stale store on a returning node is replaced, not merged), and builds on the inherited version with those entries taken out; write plans (dry run, overrides, Pi-hole import) merge onto that base. An older primary's blob (no rows) changes nothing and a write to an entry the node serves but doesn't hold answers 409 with the reason instead of a bare 404 (the UI's error note shows the server's text).
  - *AC:* (1) after a failover the new primary dry-runs, deletes and edits every API-added entry of every kind (`clu_015_promoted_primary_edits_and_deletes_every_api_entry`: upstream, upstream group, list, group, device, record, forward, rule and the replaced section `ratelimit`); (2) none is lost or resurrected across failover and failback, and a returning node's stale rows are replaced, even when the inherited blob's hash was adopted before (`clu_015_readoption_after_a_demotion_even_for_the_same_blob`); (3) an older primary's blob changes nothing (`clu_010_a_blob_without_the_rows_is_left_alone`; superseded by the `clu_015_t24_40_*` tests, T24.40); (4) `deploy/cluster3/e2e.sh` step h: add an upstream on the lease holder, kill it, delete it on the new primary, bring the old one back, it stays deleted.
  - *Done 2026-11-18 (branch fix/t24.37-managed-after-failover, ADR-1016 Proposed):* all of the above in `crates/wrendns/src/managed_adopt.rs` (new), `node_managed.rs`, `replication.rs`, `api_backend.rs` (`plan_files`, `served_not_stored`), `pihole_import.rs`, and `State::replace_managed` in `wrendns-store`. No new dependency (image delta: code only), no UI control (no setting, route or tool added), no help topic (no behaviour a user configures; the new 409 text shows in the existing error notes). The other kinds (lists, groups, devices, records, forwards, routes, routers, exclusions, upstream groups, the singletons) go through the same path and the test covers one of each shape; the node-managed kinds (OIDC providers, sinks, OTLP, guarded) already had their own adoption (T23.10).
  - *Review fixes 2026-11-18 (ADR-1016):* the adoption marker moved into `state.db` (`meta`, same transaction as the rows) under a process-wide lock and cached per process (no blob read on every tick; a failed marker write can't re-adopt); `node_only` rows are not published; the 409 reason covers records, forwards, rules, alerts, schedules, mutes and Kubernetes map rules (devices are not a write kind here, so unchanged); the 'defined in the config files' hint names the cluster configuration on a promoted primary; the override-of-an-old-file-entry limit is documented in ADR-1016, not fixed (the version no longer holds the file's own entry). Evidence wording corrected: with adoption off, `clu_015_promoted_primary_edits_and_deletes_every_api_entry` fails at its row-count assertion (the promoted node holds 0 upstream rows instead of 2), before the DELETE; the 404 `no pihole-1` is the owner's report, not that test's output.
  - *Gap found 2026-11-18 (live cluster) and closed by T24.40 (ADR-1019):* the case "an older primary's blob changes nothing" left a node promoted from an older version serving entries it did not hold, and its writes would have dropped them. Such a node now adopts what it serves (and refuses writes until it has); `clu_010_a_blob_without_the_rows_is_left_alone` was replaced by the `clu_015_t24_40_*` tests.
  - *Open:* the three-node Docker run of `deploy/cluster3/e2e.sh` with the new step was not run here (CPU budget; run it after the merge); the first failover after every node is upgraded is the first that hands entries over (a version published by an older primary has no rows), documented in ADR-1016.

- [x] **T24.44 Redirect port 80 to HTTPS.** [owner 2026-11-19] *(API-003, API-902, OBS-020; ADR-914, ADR-956, ADR-1053 (Proposed 2026-11-19))* When the UI and API listen on 443 with TLS (as the test Pis now do), plain `http://host/` on port 80 should send the browser to HTTPS.
  - *Decision (owner):* `[api] http_redirect`: off by default, or an address such as `"0.0.0.0:80"`. When set, WrenDNS opens a second, plain-HTTP listener there that answers every request with a 308 to `https://<the request's Host without its port>[:<api port if not 443>]<path and query>`, validating Host against a safe pattern (a hostname or IP, no CRLF, no userinfo; anything else gets a 400) so it can't become an open redirect beyond this host. `/livez`, `/readyz` and `/healthz` answer as on the API port. No other content; responses minimal with no-store headers. Valid only together with `[api] tls`, otherwise a validation error. It binds with `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` (the systemd unit already has it); a bind failure is logged without affecting DNS or the API. Helm and Compose: document only (no default ports). Listener checks include the redirect listener (an http GET of `/livez` expecting 200, and of `/` expecting 308). UI: Settings, System (where `[api] tls` is shown), a field under the guarded-change flow, a help topic, and docs in `docs/running.md`'s "HTTPS without a proxy" section with an example and the systemd note. Tests: Rust unit tests for Host validation and the redirect target (with and without a port, IPv6 literals, a bad Host), an integration test with TLS and the redirect on loopback ports checking the 308 and the health endpoints, and Playwright for the setting's form (dry run and guarded flow).
  - *Done 2026-11-19 (branch feat/api-http-redirect, ADR-1053 Proposed):* `ApiConfig.http_redirect` (`Option<SocketAddr>`, validated in `wrendns-config`: needs `[api] tls`, port 1 to 65535, not `[api] listen`); `crates/wrendns/src/http_redirect.rs` (`host_only`, `target`, the router with the health routes behind `only_allowed`, a 308 fallback, `no-store`), started in `server.rs` after the API binds (a bind failure only warns; a reload that changes it is listed as needing a restart); the guarded row `api-http-redirect` (`staged`, `HttpRedirect` applier: dry run with the port-below-1024 warning, overlay only next to TLS; the end-to-end build warns instead of refusing when TLS is off); probes `api-redirect` (`/livez` 200, `/` 308) excluded from the DNS-listener health rule; UI: the field in the guarded card on Settings -> System, help topic `api-http-redirect`; `docs/running.md`, `docs/recovery.md`, `docs/config-schema.json`, the support classify table. Tests: `api_003_redirect_host_*` and `api_003_redirect_target_*` (unit), `api_003_redirect_dry_run` and `api_003_redirect_overlay_needs_tls`, `api_003_the_http_redirect_is_checked`, `api_003_http_redirect_needs_tls` (config), `tests/http_redirect.rs` (TLS plus the redirect on loopback ports: 308 with the API's port, 400 for bad Hosts, health routes, a failed bind leaves DNS answering), Playwright `7-guarded2-redirect.spec.ts` (dry run, refusals, help, the guarded staged flow). Deferred: nothing; Helm and Compose are documented only. UI size 509.8 of 512 KiB gzipped. Image delta: none (no new dependency). The API port's own same-port 307 redirect still echoes the raw Host header; hardening it with the new validator is a follow-up for the owner to schedule (ADR-1053).

- [x] **T24.41 A replica shows the primary's router data.** [owner report 2026-11-19, a 3-node cluster] *(API-013, API-016, API-010, CLU-002, CLU-004, ADR-903 section 1, ADR-125; ADR-1025 (Accepted 2026-11-19))* **Owner report:** the UniFi router is an API-managed entry with a stored credential, so only the primary reads it. Device names reach replicas (`devices.names`), but the networks do not: on a replica the Networks page listed only its own interfaces (eth0, wlan0, eth0.30) instead of UniFi's LAN, vlan-30 and vlan-40, with no VLAN, gateway, DHCP pool or domain, the network drawer's device list was empty, and the Routers page said "Not read on this node (the primary)" with 0 devices, 0 networks and no last poll. - [x] **T24.35 Query log exclusions and an unlogged health check.** [owner request 2026-11-18] *(OBS-903, OPS-901, OBS-022, OBS-020, OPS-006, API-007, API-901, AGT-001..005; ADR-1014)* Seen on a cluster: the query log fills with client 127.0.0.1, group default, name localhost, because keepalived's check (every 2 s) and a watchdog (every 5 s) ask the node for `localhost`, and the node's own lookups show as 127.0.0.1 too.
  - **1. Log-only exclusions.** `[exclusions.log]` (`clients`: addresses, networks or device names; `domains`: exact or `*.` wildcard; `own_lookups`: loopback and the node's addresses), checked on the aggregator thread when the event is written (a flag check and a few hash lookups, nothing on the answer path), counted in `wrendns_queries_log_excluded_total`. They stay in the dashboard, top lists, anomalies and `/metrics` (ADR-1014; `[exclusions]` still removes from both).
  - **2. An unlogged readiness check.** `GET /readyz` on the API (and metrics) listener answers 200 only when the node's first UDP listener answers a query for the probe name on loopback (1.5 s timeout, the answer reused for 1 s, no sign-in, no configuration in the body; 503 `dns_unanswered` otherwise). `wrendns health` (existing, default URL `/readyz`) is the CLI. `deploy/keepalived/check-wrendns.sh`, its README and `docs/running.md` use it.
  - **3. The Pi-hole importer** maps `webserver.api.excludeDomains` and `excludeClients` (v6 regexes in the plain forms `^name$`, `^.*\.suffix$`, `^1\.2\.3\.4$`) and `API_EXCLUDE_DOMAINS` and `API_EXCLUDE_CLIENTS` (v5) onto `[exclusions.log]`, lists them in the preview notes, and names what it could not map.
  - *UI:* Settings, Query handling, "Kept out of the log" gains the three "Log only" fields and a summary (`ConfigEditor` edits dotted keys), help topic `qlog-exclusions`. API: the `log` object of `PUT /api/v1/exclusions/default`; MCP `plan_set_exclusions` (`log`).
  - *AC:* (1) a log-excluded query never reaches the log's sink but is counted in the analytics (`obs_903_log_exclusions_keep_queries_out_of_the_log_only`); (2) the matchers: exact, wildcard (not its apex), networks, device references (`obs_903_log_exclusions_match`); (3) config to filter: device names to the configured client, `own_lookups` covers loopback and node addresses, a bad entry is refused (`obs_903_log_exclusions_from_config`); (4) `/readyz` asks the listener, reuses the answer, says only why it failed and the probe name is what is asked (`ops_901_readyz_asks_the_listener`); (5) the importer (`obs_903_pihole_excluded_domains_and_clients`); (6) Playwright `obs_903 log-only exclusions from Settings` and `ops_901 readyz asks the listener and is never logged`; (7) OpenAPI, config schema, MCP snapshot, `api-types.ts` regenerated; `check:help` clean.
  - *Done 2026-11-18 (branch feat/t24.35-qlog-exclusions, ADR-1014 Proposed):* all of the above. No new dependency (image size delta: code only). Decisions in ADR-1014: the settings live under the shared `[exclusions]` section, not the node-local `[telemetry.qlog]` (no editable kind exists for it until T27.5, and a cluster's nodes should agree); the check asks `probe.wrendns.invalid` (the existing OBS-020 probe name, which the log and analytics already skip) rather than `localhost`, because a query carries no flag; the probe is still counted in the raw `wrendns_queries_total`, as the watchdog's is, since that counter is on the answer path; `own_lookups` is off by default. `make bench-smoke` on Docker Desktop (one UDP `bind()` takes 21 ms here) gave no verdict: cache-hot 105 qps with 37.7% loss and miss-heavy 7 qps, the host's limits (bench/README.md), and the harness fails the gates for the same reason on any change. The change touches no answer-path code: the telemetry change is one extra `Option` check per drained event on the aggregator thread, and `/readyz` runs outside the query path.
