- [x] **T24.38 Replicas stay linked to each other.** [owner report 2026-11-18] *(CLU-001, CLU-005, CLU-009, OBS-010, API-011; ADR-1018 (Proposed))* **Seen** on a 3-node cluster (node-a replica, node-b replica, node-c primary, automatic failover, 3 eligible voters) right after a rolling upgrade between two builds in the order node-a, node-b, node-c: before it, node-a reported `failover.reachableVoters` 3 for hours; after it, 2, with node-b `connected=false link=inbound`, and node-b's log repeating `linked to a peer` (node-a), `the primary answers again; leaving this node to move back to it`, `linked to a peer` (node-c) every 1 to 2 minutes.
  - **Cause (reproduced, `net_tests::voters_linked`).** Two nodes can have several streams between them at once: the main link a replica dials, the stream the voter mesh keeps (the node with the lower ID dials, ADR-056), and the one the peer dialed. The cluster kept one outbox entry per peer, so a newer stream replaced an older one's entry; and any stream's end marked the peer `connected = false` and purged the outbox. After a rolling restart, replicas that fell back to each other while the primary restarted and then moved back to it (`primary_is_back`) left the stream to the other replica; that end set the other replica `connected = false` and dropped its outbox entry, though the mesh stream between them was still open. The mesh does not dial a peer whose stream task is still running, and the page counts `connected`, so the voter link stayed lost (`reachableVoters` 2) until a restart: a stream alive but not listed. A main link left by `primary_is_back` is a cancelled read that also ran no clean-up. T24.26 (ADR-990) and T24.33 (ADR-1011) did not touch the dial or stream code (the `git diff` from the older build in `net.rs` adds only the lease-lapse and voter-reply bookkeeping): the defect is older, and a cluster that is not restarted in that order never meets it, which is why the hours before the upgrade were clean.
  - **Fix.** (1) A peer's streams are listed side by side in the outbox, each removed only when it ends; RPCs use the newest open one. (2) A peer is `connected` while it has any open stream (a count from the first frame the cluster accepts, a Hello, to the end of the stream, kept by a drop guard so a cancelled read counts too; the count is changed under the members lock and a heartbeat also sets `connected`, so a stale stream end is healed by the next heartbeat; a narrow window remains in which an old stream's end clears `connected` between a new Hello and its count, costing one spurious recorded drop); it is marked disconnected and the `disconnected` event written only when the last one ends. (3) The end of a main link is logged at info with how long it lasted and why (`cluster: the main link ended`). (3b) A main link to the primary that was up more than 3 s and then ended is redialed (primary's URLs first, after 0.2 to 1 s; a powered-off primary host can cost up to the 10 s connect timeout per URL before the replica fallback, which delays only config sync) instead of falling through to a replica, which `primary_is_back` would have to undo: one drop is no longer a detour (`dial`). A voter-mesh stream ending no longer clears the main-link record (`take_if` only for the main link). The link-drop record forgets peers whose newest drop is over an hour old and a removed node's. (4) The Cluster page: the Failover line shows a warning naming each voter whose link dropped three or more times in ten minutes (`failover.unstableVoters`), the Health tab has a `voter_links` check with a fix, and the help topic `voter-links` explains it.
  - **Tests.** `wrendns-cluster`: `clu_005_t24_38_replicas_then_primary_restart_keeps_every_voter_linked` and `..._primary_then_replicas_restart_...` (three eligible voters in automatic failover, each node on its own runtime so a stop drops its connections like a process exit; the reported order and the old order; afterwards every node reaches 3 of 3 voters, no main link moves, no link dropped twice; then the primary is killed and a survivor is elected within the lease time plus 20 s, the other follows it, no flapping), `clu_005_t24_38_a_peer_with_two_streams_stays_linked_until_the_last_ends`, `clu_005_t24_38_one_drop_of_the_primary_link_does_not_detour_through_a_replica` (a test hook cuts a replica's main link three times; a test-only counter of dials to a node that is not the primary must not move and the replica returns to the primary; the counter is read rather than sampling `connected_primary`, because `primary_is_back` undoes a detour within about 100 ms in test builds; checked to fail with the redial turned off), `clu_005_t24_38_a_refused_hello_records_no_drop_and_heartbeat_reconnects`, `clu_005_t24_38_link_drops_are_pruned`. `wrendns`: `clu_005_t24_38_voter_links_check_names_a_voter_that_comes_and_goes`. Playwright (`1-ui.spec.ts`): `clu_005 a voter whose link comes and goes is a warning on the Cluster page`. `deploy/cluster3/e2e.sh` step **j** (1 minute by default, `J_WATCH_S`, of `reachableVoters` = `voters` after the rolling restart in the reported order, no `leaving this node` lines, then the primary is killed and a survivor elected). Which tests fail on the base: the reported-order restart test (`replicas_then_primary`: `reachableVoters` stuck at 2 after the restarts) fails; `primary_then_replicas` passes on the base too (kept as a guard for the old order); the one-drop test fails without the redial (checked by turning the redial off). Step j was not shown to fail on an old image.
  - **Done 2026-11-18.** No dependency added; no DNS hot-path crate changed (`wrendns-cluster` is not one of the bench-smoke crates), so `make bench-smoke` was not run. The reviewer ran step j end to end (every step a to j passed; replica-b killed, replica-a elected 8.6 s later, 0 of 789 queries lost). The cluster3 image now builds with its own cache scope (`BUILD_CACHE_SCOPE=-cluster3`, `CLUSTER3_CACHE_SCOPE` to override) after a shared cache gave a false compile error. One end of the main link to the primary made `dial` move to a replica at once and `primary_is_back` pull it back; the one-drop test counts those detours and fails without the redial (checked), so the detour is fixed, but it is a mechanism of the cycle, not its cause; **what ends the main link to the primary every 1 to 2 minutes is still unknown** and is tracked as T24.38a below (node-b's log from the affected cluster with the `cluster: the main link ended` lines is needed).
  - **Amended 2026-11-18 (ADR-1018 decision 6).** The cluster3 run of the integration branch failed step j with `primary reports a voter whose link comes and goes` (3 drops, the last 82 s ago, before the watch window): every `voters_ok` sample passed, but the step's own rolling restart (and step i's) counted as link drops, so every planned rolling upgrade would warn for ten minutes. A drop now counts only when the peer comes back as the same process (`Hello.instance`, tag 13, a random id per start); a restarted, upgraded or gracefully stopped peer is forgotten at its Hello, an older peer without the field counts as before. Tests: `clu_005_t24_38_a_restarted_peer_is_not_an_unstable_link` (three restarts in ten minutes: no drop counted) and `clu_005_t24_38_three_drops_of_a_live_peer_are_an_unstable_link`; step j keeps its `unstableVoters == []` check, which now covers the fixed semantics.

## M23 — Secrets and integrations in the UI (owner request 2026-11-16) [fork #13]

Anything set up through a secret file can also be entered in the UI, and the files keep working and win. Values are write-only, encrypted per node and replicated to full members (ADR-903). Nothing changes on the query path, and no crate is added. Every task records its image delta (`deploy/image/size.py --oci`) against a milestone total of at most 0.10 MiB.

Order:
1. T23.1 ships first, with no behavior change.

The test has no other test sharing its ports in its binary. `wait_sign_in` now fails at once if the node's process exited, and on a timeout names the stage (before the metrics bind; metrics up but the API not, i.e. the auth store opening; API up and refusing), the last answer, the tries, and the node log's last lines with the log's age, so the next occurrence says where startup stopped. ## M22 — Network inventory and home integrations (fork owner request 2026-11-16)
In the fork `nbacheller/wrendns`: the IP and DNS side of a small network, without a DHCP server (ADR-091 stands). The routers and Home Assistant already know the devices; WrenDNS names them in DNS, shows the networks they sit in, and stays read-only toward both. Off by default; nothing new on the query path but one branch (and, when on, one lock-free load). A Home Assistant custom integration that reads this API lives outside the binary (`integrations/home-assistant/` in the fork's bundle), so it never touches the DNS path. M25 continues it with SNMP, more gateway reads and imported scans (ADR-907).

- [x] **T22.1 Device names in DNS.** *(DNS-023, DNS-010, API-010, CLU-002; ADR-901)* `[local] device_domain`, `device_ttl` (60), `device_mdns`; `device_label`; the device-name table (`device_dns.rs`, rebuilt every 10 s off the query path, follows reloads); the pipeline answers it after local records and a zone's own records, before a zone's NXDOMAIN; explain; `dnsName` on leases.
  - *AC:* (1) a router's, Home Assistant's, or named device's name answers A and PTR, authoritatively; (2) a `[[record]]` and a zone's own record for the same name win; (3) a device name inside a zone answers, other names in the zone are still NXDOMAIN; (4) off, the table is ignored; (5) two devices with one label: the named device, then router, then mDNS, then the lowest address keeps it; a CIDR client's name never becomes a device name; (6) `local` is refused as the domain; (7) `wpad`, `isatap`, and `localhost` are never device names.
  - *Done 2026-11-16:* `wrendns_policy::{device_label, LocalData::from_device_names}`, `ClientTable::{by_exact_ip, by_exact_mac, exact_ips}`, `crates/wrendns/src/device_dns.rs`, `Pipeline::device_names`, `Policy::device_dns`, the `local_answer`/`zone_answer` order, `answered_early` (explain; simulation passes none: device names follow the routers, not the simulated configuration). Tests: `dns_023_*` (label, table, settings, names from every source, the pipeline order), config validation; `deploy/routers-e2e.sh` asks real DNS for three device names and a PTR.
  - *Open:* IPv6 (done in T24.8); `bench-smoke` on quiet hardware (T24.3 has Docker Desktop numbers, which can't give a verdict); UI: the settings are T24.13 and `dnsName` on the Clients page is T24.14.

## M21 — Hangs: a watchdog and debug files (GitHub issue #7)
The owner held 0.7.0 for this (2026-11-16): the reply on #7 promised "debug symbols with 0.7.0, and a watchdog so a wedged node restarts itself and leaves a dump".

- [x] **T21.1 Debug files for every build.** *(OPS-013, NFR-005; ADR-164)* The Dockerfile links once with line tables and splits the output into the stripped binary and `wrendns.debug`; every release and edge build publishes `wrendns-<arch>-linux.debug.zst` under the signed `SHA256SUMS`.
  - *AC:* (1) the shipped binary keeps `.dep-v0` (cargo-auditable), has a `.gnu_debuglink`, and runs as before; (2) the debug file holds the symbol table and line tables, and `addr2line -e wrendns.debug` resolves an address of the stripped binary to a function and line; (3) bench-smoke A/B (five alternating rounds) shows no regression; (4) the image workflow publishes the three debug files, `SHA256SUMS` lists them and `verify.sh` checks them; (5) the size gate still passes; (6) the docs say how to read a stack with it.
  - *Done 2026-11-16:* the Dockerfile links once with line tables and splits with `llvm-objcopy` (the debug file is kept out of `/out`, which the image copies whole); `image.yml` publishes `wrendns-<arch>-linux.debug.zst` (zstd 10, 21 to 25 MB) under the signed sums; `verify.sh` checks them and nightly warns if two debug files differ. Measured on the build VM with the real Docker build: the shipped binary is 5,232 bytes larger (not byte-identical code), `bench-smoke` ten alternating runs each shows no regression (cache-hot median 531k and 527k qps, miss-heavy p50 217 and 223 µs), and the images grew by about 0.04 MiB (amd64 14.70 MiB of the 15 MiB gate: the margin is 0.30 MiB). Checked on the published edge build 0.7.0-edge.369: the three files are in `SHA256SUMS`, the binary's debuglink CRC matches the downloaded debug file, and `addr2line` resolves a watchdog function to `watchdog.rs:519`.
  - *Open:* `verify.sh`'s debug-file check runs on a stable release only, so its first run is the 0.7.0 tag's build; a build ID (the zig linker writes none).
- [x] **T21.2 The watchdog.** *(OPS-012, OPS-006, CLU-004; ADR-163)* `[watchdog]` (node-local, restart-only), a thread outside the runtime that checks that the runtime runs a task and that the node's own UDP listener answers `probe.wrendns.invalid`, writes a dump and exits with status 70 after `stall_secs` without a pass, with a restart limit; metrics; the newest dump in the support package; docs.
  - *AC:* (1) a stuck runtime is seen and a healthy or busy one isn't; (2) the stall is dumped once, the restart is limited per hour, `action = "dump"` never exits; (3) the dump is `0640` in a `0750` directory, the newest five kept; (4) the probe is asked of a real listener and any answer passes; (5) nothing is added to the query path; (6) a real process built with `wedge-test` is dumped and exits with status 70, and the next run says why (`deploy/watchdog/e2e.sh`, in CI).
  - *Done 2026-11-16:* `[watchdog]` (node-local, restart-only), `watchdog.rs` (the tracker, the two checks, the restart limit, the dump and its rotation, the metrics), the newest dump in the support package, docs and the FAQ, and `deploy/watchdog/e2e.sh` in CI (it passed there on the stripped `bench-fast` build). Tests: 22 in `watchdog_tests.rs`, config limits, the package. A `support_log` rotation test no longer trusts a two-second flush.
  - *Open:* the reporter's own hang has no known cause yet (the watchdog and the stacks are how the next one is read); a systemd `WatchdogSec` integration; the dump's build ID.
- [x] **T21.3 Stacks in the dump.** *(OPS-012, NFR-003; ADR-163)* Each thread reports its own return addresses when the watchdog signals it (`wrendns-net::stacks`, the only `unsafe`, no new crate).
  - *AC:* (1) a blocked thread's stack holds its own function; (2) a thread that can't answer is listed as not answering within the 5 s wait; (3) a second capture works; (4) the dump's addresses resolve with the debug file (the e2e on a debug build).

On **arm64** the CI test job (a real aarch64 runner) runs the two stack tests and passes them: a blocked thread's stack holds its own function there too (checked 2026-11-16 on `73ba8f2`).

(1) Check (h) had killed a replica, because check (h) turned automatic failover on after the primary had been deposed by an election the test itself caused (the product issue below); now failover is on from the bring-up, and the node that holds the lease (`wrendns_cluster_lease_held` 1) is killed, with the promotion required 5 to 40 s later. (2, 3) The runtime's own worker count is logged (`runtime_workers`) and asserted (2 on replica-a); the thread count against a 24-CPU host is gone. (4) Every host port is bound to `127.0.0.1`. (5) Check (e) writes `worker_memory_mib = 48` and reads it back on replica-b. (6) The rolling-restart monitor is a daemon stopped in a `finally`, and each restart has a 120 s timeout. (7) The failover probe fails on any timeout or on more than 1% unanswered queries. (8) The CI time limit is 60 minutes. (9) `set-failover auto` prints a warning, and `docs/running.md` says to turn it on before the replicas join. (10) Check (d) asserts 200 on every read surface. (11) The CI paths cover `cluster.rs`, `forward.rs`, `settings_kinds.rs`, `managed.rs`, `api_backend.rs`, `main.rs`, `wrendns-store`, `wrendns-config` and `Cargo.lock`. (12, part) The key-share send is one tested decision (`clu_005_c`), and an unchanged pending CA key isn't rewritten (`clu_005_b`); the refusal WARN is still repeated (Open, item (b)). (13) An interrupted run unpauses the primary before it tears down. Found on the way, fixed: a `[discovery]` the primary sets was refused by every replica at its defaults (ADR-948 addendum, CLU-010, `clu_010_a_discovery_section_is_shared_both_ways`); and a fresh election stood at once against a primary whose lease was not yet granted, so the primary now stands first and a replica waits one lease period (ADR-947 addendum, `clu_005_d`). Tests: `wrendns-cluster` 64 unit and 1 integration pass with `--test-threads=1`; `wrendns-config` all pass; the `wrendns` binary's 591 unit tests pass; `fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean on both crates. Final run, the committed `deploy/cluster3/e2e.sh` unmodified (exit 0, 3 min 36 s, from a cold cluster; the image built first); a second run on the merged tree also passed (exit 0, 3 min 28 s, replica-a promoted 11.6 s after the kill): (a) three connected nodes; (b) the record answered on all three within 1.7 s; (c) forwarded; (d) the secret readable on both replicas, its value on no read surface or log, every read surface 200; (e) the router on all three, the first `[discovery]` write accepted with all up and with replica-b stopped, and replica-b reads 48 MiB; (f) 18 queries in the primary's log, 6 from replica-a; (g) twenty concurrent reads at replica-a with the primary paused, all 200, the slowest 3.5 s; DNS 491 queries, 0 timeouts; `/livez` 7 of 7, `/metrics` 7 of 7; replica-a `runtime_workers=2`, the primary `runtime_workers=24`; the pause lapsed the primary's lease, and replica-a was promoted (the cluster doing its job); (h) the lease holder replica-a killed, replica-b promoted 8.76 s later, 0 SERVFAIL, loss 0.00% (0 of 1574), the edit reaches the other survivor, and replica-a, started again, steps down and follows; (i) at least two of three nodes answer at every one of 50 samples while each node is restarted in turn.

The CLI warns and `docs/running.md` says to turn it on before the replicas join; the product fix is the owner's choice (the running primary adopting the mode without a restart, or a replica not standing against a primary whose records say `manual`). It needs a fork issue (not filed from this track) and an ADR (fork ADRs 947 and 948 are this track's, both in use). (b) The refused key share is still repeated every 30 s until the peer learns the new primary, and the receiver logs the refusal each time (review 12). Stopping that needs per-stream state; not fixed here. (c) *Fixed after the merge:* `wrendns-cluster`'s parallel run failed with "Connection refused" because each test slept a fixed 100 ms before connecting; the tests now wait until the listener accepts (`listening()` in `net_tests.rs`), and six parallel `-j 4` runs pass. (d) A survivor's poll in check (h) got no 200 once in the runs (the first failed run); signing in again before the kill fixed it, and the probe now reports each survivor's poll status. The cause isn't pinned down: a session that lapsed when that node stepped down during (g) is the likely one.

(2) The owner's wording of check (f) names `/api/v1/clients`, which lists configured devices and has no node labels; the check uses `/api/v1/stats/top?kind=clients&scope=node:<name>`. - [x] **T21.7 Turning on automatic failover in a running cluster is safe.** *(CLU-005; ADR-947 addendum, T21.5 open (a); a new fork ADR)* Owner decision 2026-11-17: the running primary adopts `auto` as soon as it signs the failover record, with no restart, and starts renewing its lease at once. A replica stands for election only after it has seen a lease from the current primary and that lease has lapsed; a primary that has never held a lease under `auto` is not deposed. Also fix T21.5 open (1): replicas in either mode report each other's health from the heartbeats they relay, so `peers_up` isn't false in manual mode. Tests: `clu_005_t21_7_a_running_primary_adopts_auto_and_is_not_deposed` (lease at the first tick, one epoch, no replica stands over 60 s of renewals), `clu_005_t21_7_a_replica_stands_only_after_a_lease_it_saw_lapses` (a replica that never saw a lease waits 600 s without asking; one that did stands once it lapses), `clu_005_t21_7_a_stored_ballot_counts_as_a_lease_seen`, `clu_001_a_replica_learns_that_another_replica_is_up_from_the_primarys_heartbeats`; Playwright `clu_005 the failover mode changes on the Cluster page without a restart` (the whole file: 167 passed). `wrendns-cluster` 72 + 1 sim test pass; `wrendns` filter `clu_ cluster maintenance failover ops_010` 98 pass; `fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` clean. `deploy/cluster3/e2e.sh` now turns failover on after the replicas join, with no restart: new check a2 (each replica reports all three up in manual mode; after `set-failover auto` all three adopt it, the primary holds a lease, keeps epoch 1 and its role for 45 s, no replica stands), and check h still passes (replica-b held the lease and was killed, replica-a promoted 9.68 s later, loss 0.00%, the old primary follows); the full run passed all checks. CI found two effects of the rule in `deploy/cluster/failover-e2e.sh`: a replica killed-for never granted the primary a renewal (the script killed the primary within 5 s of the join), and a deposed primary whose successor died before it had granted that successor a renewal never stood (its own old lease refuses renewals for a lease period); the second is fixed in the rule (a ballot for itself plus a newer epoch counts as a lease seen, `clu_005_t21_7_a_stored_ballot_counts_as_a_lease_seen`), and both older scripts now wait for the replica's first renewal. T21.5 open (a) and open (1) are closed. Image delta: no dependency added, 0. No hot-path crate changed (`wrendns-cluster` and the binary only), so no `bench-smoke`.

(2) A primary rebuilt by a voter change pauses publishing for one round trip (it resumes with no lease). (3) The Docker build's shared cargo cache keys on file mtimes: after another track's build, a changed crate can be taken as fresh; touching the changed sources before the run (as done here) works around it.
